A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a scalable quantum platform.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new defect platform in wide-band-gap oxides for quantum technologies, overcoming limitations of existing systems like NV centers.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and readout fidelity.
result: The defect exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a promising new platform for scalable quantum technologies, combining long coherence with high-fidelity readout.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or require full characterization, which is impractical. A method to integrate realistic device characterization into rigorous security proofs is needed for practical QKD certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that combines device characterization data with entropy accumulation or similar techniques to produce composable security bounds, accounting for device imperfections.
result: The framework yields tight security bounds that incorporate device parameters, enabling certification of QKD systems with realistic devices.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device implementations, facilitating standards and certification for quantum key distribution.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can significantly boost logical performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity flips, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasures.
result: The erasure conversion scheme yields a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to error suppression via erasure conversion, enhancing prospects for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are typically limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: The authors propose and analyze a scheme where multiple cavity modes are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging spatial mode separation.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms that can be processed in parallel without crosstalk, enabling fast entangling gates and readout.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced operations in neutral-atom quantum computers, addressing a key bottleneck.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity gates and readout simultaneously is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but crosstalk and calibration challenges often limit performance.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize errors across all operations in a fixed-frequency transmon qubit architecture.
result: They report single-qubit gate fidelity >99.9%, two-qubit gate fidelity >99.9%, and readout fidelity >99.9% on the same device, with low crosstalk.
conclusion: This work shows that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible in superconducting qubits, removing a major obstacle to building larger quantum processors.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, introducing new stabilizer states and error-correcting codes for continuous-variable and discrete-variable hybrid platforms.
motivation: Hybrid quantum processors combining continuous-variable (oscillator) and discrete-variable (qudit) systems are promising for quantum information processing, but lack a unified stabilizer formalism for error correction and state characterization.
method: The authors develop a symplectic formalism over rings to describe hybrid systems, define stabilizer states and codes using noncommutative geometry, and construct scalable error-correcting codes.
result: New classes of hybrid stabilizer states and codes are presented, including codes that can correct errors on both oscillator and qudit components, with potential applications in displacement sensing.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational framework for hybrid quantum processors, enabling systematic error correction and state manipulation in mixed continuous-discrete variable systems.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative evolution that mixes rapidly while maintaining accuracy.
result: The local circuit approach achieves polynomial mixing time and high-fidelity Gibbs state preparation, with rigorous bounds on convergence and error.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable method for quantum Gibbs sampling, advancing quantum simulation and thermodynamic computing.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise, establishing fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the impact of Markovian noise on quantum memories is crucial for practical quantum information processing, yet the fundamental limits of storage and error correction under such noise were not fully characterized.
method: The authors employ quantum information theory, including entropy measures and channel capacities, to analyze the effects of Markovian noise on quantum memory. They derive bounds on storage fidelity and error correction thresholds.
result: They derive tight bounds on the achievable storage fidelity and error correction thresholds for quantum memories subject to Markovian noise, revealing trade-offs between memory size, noise strength, and error correction overhead.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits that guide the design of quantum memories and error correction protocols, highlighting the necessity of active error correction for long-term storage under Markovian noise.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, bridging scales from stochastic to macroscopic thermodynamics.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: Constructs a local decoder for the 2D toric code that preserves logical state for exponential time under circuit-level noise without non-local classical computation.
motivation: The 2D toric code is a promising topological quantum memory, but existing decoders require non-local classical processing, limiting practical implementation. A fully local decoder would enable fault-tolerant quantum computation with minimal overhead.
method: Uses ideas from hierarchical classical cellular automata (Tsirelson and Gács) to design a circuit of strictly local quantum operations that acts as a decoder for the toric code.
result: The decoder maintains a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise, and the construction can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes.
conclusion: This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: The paper generalizes classical Doeblin coefficients to quantum channels, providing efficiently computable bounds on contraction coefficients with applications to quantum machine learning, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients give strong data-processing inequalities, but a quantum generalization was lacking. The authors aim to define quantum Doeblin coefficients with desirable properties and interpret them in terms of entanglement and state exclusion.
method: Several quantum Doeblin coefficients are defined, one of which is multiplicative and efficiently computable. They are interpreted as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations, using both entanglement-assisted and unassisted settings.
result: The quantum Doeblin coefficients provide upper bounds on trace-distance contraction coefficients, leading to improved bounds on noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation, sample complexity of hypothesis testing, and mixing times of quantum channels.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are a versatile tool for analyzing quantum channels, offering computational efficiency and broad applicability across quantum information processing tasks.

title: Performance Guarantees For Quantum Neural Estimation Of Entropies
authors: Sreejith Sreekumar, Ziv Goldfeld, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2113 (2026).

Estimating quantum entropies and divergences is an important problem in quantum physics, information theory, and machine learning. Quantum neural estimators (QNEs), which utilize a hybrid classical-quantum architecture, have recently emerged as an appealing computational framework for estimating these measures. Such estimators combine classical neural networks with parametrized quantum circuits, and their deployment typically entails tedious tuning of hyperparameters controlling the sample size, network architecture, and circuit topology. This work initiates the study of formal guarantees for QNEs of measured (Rényi) relative entropies in the form of non-asymptotic error risk bounds. We further establish exponential tail bounds showing that the error is sub-Gaussian and thus sharply concentrates about the ground truth value. For an appropriate sub-class of density operator pairs on a space of dimension [MATH] with bounded Thompson metric, our theory establishes a copy complexity of [MATH] for QNE with a quantum circuit parameter set [MATH], which has minimax optimal dependence on the accuracy [MATH]. Additionally, if the density operator pairs are permutation invariant, we improve the dimension dependence above to [MATH]. Our theory aims to facilitate principled implementation of QNEs for measured relative entropies and guide hyperparameter tuning in practice.

.
tldr: Provides non-asymptotic error bounds and exponential tail bounds for quantum neural estimators of measured Rényi relative entropies, with minimax optimal copy complexity.
motivation: Quantum neural estimators (QNEs) are a promising hybrid classical-quantum approach for estimating entropies and divergences, but lack formal performance guarantees, making hyperparameter tuning heuristic.
method: Derives non-asymptotic error risk bounds and exponential tail bounds for QNEs of measured Rényi relative entropies, using concentration inequalities and covering number arguments.
result: Establishes copy complexity O(|Θ|/ε^2) for general density operators with bounded Thompson metric, improving to O(log(d)/ε^2) under permutation invariance, both minimax optimal in ε.
conclusion: The theoretical guarantees enable principled implementation and hyperparameter selection for QNEs, advancing reliable entropy estimation in quantum information.

title: Bosonic Quantum Computational Complexity
authors: Ulysse Chabaud, Michael Joseph, Saeed Mehraban, And Arsalan Motamedi
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2110 (2026).

Quantum computing involving physical systems with continuous degrees of freedom, such as the quantum states of light, has recently attracted significant interest. However, a well-defined quantum complexity theory for these bosonic computations over infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces is missing. In this work, we lay foundations for such a research program. We introduce natural complexity classes and problems based on bosonic generalizations of BQP, the local Hamiltonian problem, and QMA. We uncover several relationships and subtle differences between standard Boolean classical and discrete variable quantum complexity classes and identify outstanding open problems. In particular: 1. We show that the power of quadratic (Gaussian) quantum dynamics is equivalent to the class BQL. More generally, we define classes of continuous-variable quantum polynomial time computations with a bounded probability of error based on higher-degree gates. Due to the infinite dimensional Hilbert space, it is not a priori clear whether a decidable upper bound can be obtained for these classes. We identify complete problems for these classes and demonstrate a BQP lower and EXPSPACE upper bound. We further show that the problem of computing expectation values of polynomial bosonic observables is in PSPACE. 2. We prove that the problem of deciding the boundedness of the spectrum of a bosonic Hamiltonian is co-NP-hard. Furthermore, we show that the problem of finding the minimum energy of a bosonic Hamiltonian critically depends on the non-Gaussian stellar rank of the family of energy-constrained states one optimizes over: for constant stellar rank, it is NP-complete; for polynomially-bounded rank, it is in QMA; for unbounded rank, it is undecidable.

.
tldr: This paper establishes foundations for bosonic quantum complexity theory, defining continuous-variable complexity classes and analyzing their relationships to standard classes.
motivation: Quantum computing with continuous variables (e.g., light) lacks a well-defined complexity theory, hindering understanding of the power and limitations of bosonic quantum computers.
method: The authors introduce bosonic generalizations of BQP, QMA, and the local Hamiltonian problem, using Gaussian and higher-degree gates, and analyze their computational power via completeness results and upper/lower bounds.
result: Gaussian quantum dynamics is equivalent to BQL; higher-degree bosonic BQP lies between BQP and EXPSPACE; the bosonic local Hamiltonian problem is NP-hard for constant stellar rank and undecidable for unbounded rank.
conclusion: Bosonic quantum complexity classes exhibit subtle differences from discrete-variable classes, with undecidability emerging for unbounded-rank Hamiltonians, highlighting the need for further research.

title: Most Incompatible Measurements And Sum-of-squares Optimisation
authors: Sébastien Designolle
abstract: Measurement incompatibility, or joint measurability, is a cornerstone of quantum theory and a useful resource. For finite-dimensional systems, quantifying this resource and establishing universal bounds valid for all measurements is a long-standing problem. In this work, we exhibit analytical universal parent measurements giving access to bounds that beat the state of the art. In particular, we can show that, for relevant robustnesses, sets of anticommuting observables give rise to the most incompatible dichotomic measurements. We also formalise the construction of such universal parent measurements in the framework of sum-of-squares optimisation and obtain preliminary numerical results demonstrating the power of the method by improving on our own analytical values. All results find direct application for demonstrating genuine high-dimensional steering, that is, certifying the dimensionality of a quantum system in a one-sided device-independent manner.
tldr: This paper identifies the most incompatible measurements using sum-of-squares optimization, with applications to high-dimensional steering.
motivation: Quantifying measurement incompatibility and establishing universal bounds is a long-standing problem in quantum theory, with implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors construct analytical universal parent measurements and formalize the problem using sum-of-squares optimization, deriving bounds that improve on state-of-the-art results.
result: They show that anticommuting observables yield the most incompatible dichotomic measurements, and numerical results further improve the analytical bounds.
conclusion: The results provide direct applications for certifying high-dimensional quantum steering in a one-sided device-independent manner.

title: Non-equilibrium Symmetry Of Cyclic First-passage Times
authors: Shiling Liang And Simone Pigolotti Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract: We study the sum of first passage times along an arbitrary cycle made up of states of a small physical system. We show that, if the system is at thermodynamic equilibrium, this sum follows the same probability distribution regardless of whether the cycle is explored clockwise or counterclockwise (CCW). Out of equilibrium, the distributions of clockwise and CCW cyclic first passage times are related by a detailed fluctuation theorem. This result descends from a symmetry of clockwise and CCW trajectories, which combines time reversal with swapping portions of the trajectories. We then relate the entropy produced along the cycle with the entropy production of the whole system using large deviation theory. Our results reveal a novel symmetry in stochastic systems, of potential broad applicability in non-equilibrium physics.
tldr: The paper reveals a symmetry in cyclic first-passage times of stochastic systems, linking clockwise and counterclockwise distributions via a fluctuation theorem out of equilibrium.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium symmetries in small systems and relate first-passage time statistics to entropy production.
method: The authors analyze first-passage times along cycles in state space, using time-reversal symmetry and large deviation theory to derive a fluctuation theorem.
result: At equilibrium, clockwise and counterclockwise first-passage time distributions are identical; out of equilibrium, they satisfy a detailed fluctuation theorem related to entropy production.
conclusion: The discovered symmetry provides a new tool for probing non-equilibrium thermodynamics and may have broad applicability in stochastic systems.

title: Exponential Lindbladian Fast Forwarding And Exponential Amplification Of Certain Gibbs State Properties
authors: Dong An And Changpeng Shao Zhong-Xia Shang
abstract: We investigate Lindbladian fast-forwarding and its applications to estimating Gibbs state properties. Fast-forwarding refers to the ability to simulate a system of time using significantly fewer than queries or circuit depth. While various Hamiltonian systems are known to circumvent the no fast-forwarding theorem, analogous results for dissipative dynamics, governed by Lindbladians, remain largely unexplored. We first present a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity up to error , improving previous algorithms. When the jump operators have certain structures (i.e. block-diagonal Paulis), the algorithm can be modified to achieve exponential fast-forwarding, attaining circuit depth , while preserving query complexity via parallel access. Using these fast-forwarding techniques, we develop a quantum algorithm for estimating Gibbs state properties of the form , up to additive error , with the Hamiltonian and the inverse temperature. For input states exhibiting certain coherence conditions—e.g. —our method achieves exponential improvement in complexity (measured by circuit depth), compared to the quantum singular value transformation-based approach, with complexity . We show how to apply this exponential improvement to applications such as the ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation. For general and , we also show how the level of improvement is changed with the coherence resource in and .
tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for fast-forwarding Lindbladian evolution and exponentially improving the estimation of Gibbs state properties under certain coherence conditions.
motivation: Simulating dissipative quantum dynamics and estimating Gibbs state properties are central to quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are limited by the no fast-forwarding theorem. The authors aim to overcome these limitations for Lindbladians with structured jump operators.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity. For block-diagonal Pauli jump operators, they modify the algorithm to achieve exponential fast-forwarding in circuit depth while preserving query complexity via parallel access. They then apply these techniques to estimate Gibbs state properties using a quantum algorithm that leverages coherence in the input state.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential improvement in circuit depth for estimating Gibbs state properties when the input state satisfies certain coherence conditions (e.g., being a pure state), compared to the quantum singular value transformation approach. The complexity scales as O(log(1/ε)) for such cases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that exponential fast-forwarding is possible for certain dissipative dynamics, leading to significant speedups for Gibbs state property estimation. This opens new avenues for quantum algorithms in thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Genuine multipartite nonlocality is a key resource for quantum information tasks, but existing tests are often noise-sensitive. A robust method is needed for practical verification.
method: The authors construct an inflated network where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities whose violation certifies genuine multipartite nonlocality.
result: The proposed approach is noise-robust and can detect genuine multipartite nonlocality under realistic noise levels, outperforming standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and robust tool for certifying genuine multipartite nonlocality, with potential applications in quantum network protocols and device-independent tasks.

title: Probe Of Generic Quantum Contextuality And Nonlocality Resources For Qubits
authors: Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, And Yan-Kui Bai
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, and Yan-Kui Bai

The authors prove that the entropic uncertainty relation with a quantum memory intrinsically connects local preparation contextuality with bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality, which is captured by two quantitative trade-off relations via a faithful criterion for the contextuality detection. They further verify the theoretical results on solid-state superconducting systems through two independent demonstrations on the Quafu quantum cloud platform.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060405] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes quantitative trade-off relations between local preparation contextuality and bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality via entropic uncertainty relations, and verifies them on a superconducting quantum cloud platform.
motivation: To understand the fundamental connections between contextuality, nonlocality, and entanglement, and to provide a faithful criterion for detecting contextuality in qubit systems.
method: The authors prove theoretical trade-off relations using entropic uncertainty relations with quantum memory, and experimentally test them on the Quafu quantum cloud platform using superconducting qubits.
result: They derive quantitative trade-off relations linking local preparation contextuality to entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality, and confirm these relations experimentally.
conclusion: The work reveals intrinsic connections between contextuality and nonlocality resources, offering a new perspective on quantum correlations and a practical detection criterion.

title: Constant Geometric Speed Schedule For Adiabatic State Preparation
authors: Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, And Sangkook Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, and Sangkook Choi

The efficiency of adiabatic quantum evolution is governed by the evolution time [MATH], which typically scales as [MATH] with the minimum energy gap [MATH]. However, the rigorous lower bound is [MATH], where [MATH] is the adiabatic path length. Al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023233] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a constant geometric speed schedule for adiabatic state preparation that achieves the optimal scaling of evolution time with the adiabatic path length, improving over conventional linear schedules.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum evolution is limited by the minimum energy gap, but the rigorous lower bound depends on the adiabatic path length. Conventional linear schedules are suboptimal, motivating the search for schedules that achieve the theoretical bound.
method: The authors derive a constant geometric speed schedule based on the geometric structure of the adiabatic path, using the concept of path length in parameter space and optimizing the evolution speed to maintain adiabaticity.
result: The proposed schedule achieves the optimal scaling of evolution time proportional to the adiabatic path length, with a constant geometric speed that minimizes the total time while satisfying the adiabatic condition.
conclusion: The constant geometric speed schedule provides a practical and optimal method for adiabatic state preparation, with implications for quantum computing and quantum thermodynamics where efficient state preparation is crucial.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem that unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroup structures, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using Clifford circuits doped with non-Clifford gates requires extensive doping, establishing a fundamental resource cost.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to achieve pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and for delineating the power of Clifford circuits.
method: The authors derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates (e.g., T gates) required for a circuit to approximate random unitaries, using techniques from quantum information theory and representation theory.
result: They show that the non-Clifford cost scales extensively with the number of qubits, meaning that a constant or sublinear number of non-Clifford gates is insufficient for pseudorandomness.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental limit on the efficiency of generating pseudorandom unitaries with doped Clifford circuits, with implications for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework establishing fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling of bosonic systems and demonstrating that non-Gaussian resources can surpass these limits.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes is crucial for quantum technologies, but Gaussian operations impose constraints; understanding and overcoming these limits is key to achieving lower temperatures.
method: The authors derive bounds on cooling using Gaussian resource theories and then show how non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can enhance cooling beyond Gaussian limits.
result: Gaussian cooling is fundamentally limited, but non-Gaussian resources enable access to colder states, quantified by new bounds and achievable protocols.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian operations provide a practical pathway to surpass Gaussian cooling limits, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and bosonic quantum computing.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: Proposes a fixed measurement setting to estimate entanglement witnesses for multipartite states, enabling measurement-based entanglement verification without changing settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are key for detecting entanglement but typically require different measurement settings; a fixed setting simplifies experimental verification.
method: Introduces 'network states' and a fixed measurement setting to estimate decomposable and non-decomposable entanglement witnesses, including for bound entangled states and graph states.
result: Shows that decomposable EWs (partial transpose criteria) can be estimated with a fixed setting, and extends to non-decomposable EWs for bound entanglement and multipartite graph states.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient, measurement-based entanglement verification in distributed quantum networks and metrology.

title: Exact Distinguishability Between Real-valued And Complex-valued Haar Random Quantum States
authors: Tristan Nemoz, Romain Alléaume, And Peter Brown
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2120 (2026).

Haar random states are fundamental objects in quantum information theory and quantum computing. We study the density matrix resulting from sampling [MATH] copies of a [MATH]-dimensional quantum state according to the Haar measure on the orthogonal group. In particular, we analytically compute its spectral decomposition. This allows us to compute exactly the trace distance between [MATH]-copies of a real Haar random state and [MATH]-copies of a complex Haar random state. Using this we show a lower-bound on the approximation parameter of real-valued state [MATH]-designs and improve the lower-bound on the number of copies required for imaginarity testing.

.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral decomposition of the density matrix of multiple copies of Haar random states from the orthogonal group, and uses it to exactly compute the trace distance between real and complex Haar random states, leading to improved lower bounds on real-valued state designs and imaginarity testing.
motivation: Understanding the distinguishability between real and complex random quantum states is fundamental for quantum information theory and quantum computing, with implications for state designs and imaginarity testing.
method: The authors analytically compute the spectral decomposition of the density matrix resulting from sampling multiple copies of a Haar random state from the orthogonal group, then compute the trace distance between real and complex Haar random states.
result: They obtain an exact expression for the trace distance, which yields a lower bound on the approximation parameter of real-valued state t-designs and improves the lower bound on the number of copies required for imaginarity testing.
conclusion: The work provides exact analytical results for distinguishing real from complex random states, advancing the theory of quantum state designs and imaginarity.

title: A Refined Frauchiger–Renner Paradox Based On Strong Contextuality
authors: Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2116 (2026).

The Frauchiger–Renner paradox derives an inconsistency when quantum theory is used to describe the use of itself, by means of a scenario where agents model other agents quantumly and reason about each other's knowledge. We observe that logical contextuality (à la Hardy) is the key ingredient of the FR paradox, and we provide a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario. In contrast to the FR paradox, this GHZ–FR paradox neither requires post-selection nor any reasoning by observers who are modelled quantumly. If one accepts the universality of quantum theory including superobservers, we propose a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve these extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.

.
tldr: The paper strengthens the Frauchiger–Renner paradox using strong contextuality from the GHZ–Mermin scenario, eliminating the need for post-selection or quantum self-reference.
motivation: To understand the foundational inconsistency in quantum theory when describing itself, and to clarify the role of contextuality in extended Wigner's friend scenarios.
method: The authors identify logical contextuality as the key ingredient of the original FR paradox and construct a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario, analyzing it without post-selection or quantum agents reasoning about each other.
result: They derive a GHZ–FR paradox that is stronger than the original, and propose an extension of Peres's dictum to resolve such paradoxes.
conclusion: Strong contextuality is central to the FR paradox, and the new paradox highlights foundational issues in quantum theory's self-consistency.

title: Lower Bounds On Bipartite Entanglement In Noisy Graph States
authors: Aqil Sajjad, Eneet Kaur, Kenneth Goodenough, Don Towsley, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2111 (2026).

Graph states are a key resource for a number of applications in quantum information theory. Due to the inherent noise in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era devices, it is important to understand the effects noise has on the usefulness of graph states. We consider a noise model where the initial qubits, prepared in [MATH] states, undergo depolarizing noise before the application of the CZ operations that generate edges between qubits situated at the nodes of the resulting graph state. For this model we develop a method for calculating the coherent information – a lower bound on the rate at which entanglement can be distilled, across a bipartition of the graph state. We also identify some patterns on how adding more nodes or edges affects the bipartite distillable entanglement. As an application, we find a family of graph states that maintain a strictly positive coherent information for any amount of (non-maximal) depolarizing noise.

.
tldr: Develops a method to compute coherent information as a lower bound on distillable entanglement for noisy graph states under depolarizing noise.
motivation: Graph states are key resources for quantum information tasks, but NISQ devices introduce noise that degrades entanglement. Understanding how noise affects distillable entanglement is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors model noise as depolarizing noise on initial qubits before CZ gate application, and derive a method to calculate coherent information across bipartitions of the graph state.
result: They identify patterns on how adding nodes or edges affects bipartite distillable entanglement, and find a family of graph states that maintain positive coherent information for any non-maximal depolarizing noise.
conclusion: The work provides tools to quantify entanglement in noisy graph states, which is important for quantum network and error correction applications.

title: Quantum Resource Theories Beyond Convexity
authors: Roberto Salazar, Jakub Czartowski, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Paweł Horodecki, And Karol Życzkowski
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2104 (2026).

A class of quantum resource theories, based on non-convex star-shape sets, presented in this work captures the key quantum properties that cannot be studied by standard convex theories. We provide operational interpretations for a resource of this class and demonstrate its advantage to improve performance of correlated quantum discrimination tasks and testing of quantum combs. Proposed techniques provide useful tools to describe quantum discord, total correlations in composite quantum systems and to estimate the degree of non-Markovianity of an analyzed quantum dynamics. Other applications include the problem of unistochasticity of a given bistochastic matrix, with relevance for quantization of classical dynamics and studies of violation of CP-symmetry in high energy physics. In all these cases, the non-linear witnesses introduced here outperform the standard linear witnesses. Importance of our findings for quantum information theory is also emphasized.

.
tldr: Introduces non-convex star-shape quantum resource theories with operational interpretations and nonlinear witnesses that outperform linear ones.
motivation: Standard convex resource theories cannot capture certain quantum properties like quantum discord and non-Markovianity; a more general framework is needed.
method: Defines resource theories based on star-shape sets, provides operational interpretations for discrimination tasks and quantum combs, and constructs nonlinear witnesses.
result: Nonlinear witnesses outperform linear witnesses in detecting quantum discord, total correlations, non-Markovianity, and unistochasticity.
conclusion: The proposed non-convex resource theories offer a powerful tool for studying quantum properties beyond convexity, with applications in quantum information theory.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom infrastructure but suffers from low secret key rates and security proofs that are not composable. The authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: They combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization of the secret key rate.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work brings CV-QKD closer to practical deployment by demonstrating high rates and rigorous security, a significant step for quantum networks.

title: Q-dice: Quantum Distributed Interconnect Compiler And Emulator
authors: Michael Silver, Zachary Vernec, Hans-Arno Jacobsen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As distributed quantum computing (DQC) offers a leading path towards scalable quantum computation, the ability to benchmark distributed algorithms under realistic conditions becomes critical for system co-design. However, without access to physical systems, researchers lack tools to evaluate distribution protocols. We introduce Q-DICE (Quantum Distributed Interconnect Compiler and Emulator), a hardware-aware emulation environment for benchmarking distributed quantum circuits on classical simulators and on NISQ-era monolithic hardware. This work provides three core contributions: (1) a programmatic scheme to construct distributed QPU backends, utilizing two novel techniques - QPU slicing and stitching - to facilitate distributed circuit mapping, (2) a methodology for modeling nonlocal link noise using physically motivated Kraus operators and stochastic error channels, and (3) a boundary-aware circuit mapping algorithm enforcing distributed QPU topology constraints during transpilation. Together, these components constitute a distribution-aware compiler and noise-modeling engine that faithfully enforces the physical limitations of distributed quantum hardware within existing execution environments. We validate Q-DICE against a multitude of experimentally demonstrated quantum circuits, including a distributed Grover's search on optically linked trapped-ion hardware, achieving a worst-case fidelity deviation of 4% between simulated and experimental results. These findings demonstrate Q-DICE's capacity to accurately reproduce real distributed quantum system behavior across platforms, streamlining experimentation with distributed quantum algorithms and architectures.
tldr: Q-DICE is a hardware-aware emulation environment for benchmarking distributed quantum circuits, providing tools for constructing distributed QPU backends, modeling nonlocal link noise, and mapping circuits under topology constraints.
motivation: Distributed quantum computing is a promising path to scalability, but researchers lack tools to evaluate distribution protocols without physical hardware.
method: The authors introduce QPU slicing/stitching for distributed circuit mapping, physically motivated Kraus operator noise models for nonlocal links, and a boundary-aware circuit mapping algorithm that enforces distributed QPU topology constraints.
result: Validation against experimental distributed Grover's search on optically linked trapped-ion hardware shows worst-case fidelity deviation of 4% between simulation and experiment.
conclusion: Q-DICE accurately reproduces real distributed quantum system behavior, enabling streamlined experimentation with distributed quantum algorithms and architectures.

title: Fisher Geometry Reshapes The Effect Of Incompatibility In Multiparameter Quantum Estimation
authors: Matteo G. A. Paris Jiayu He
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiparameter quantum estimation faces two fundamental obstacles: sloppiness, i.e., anisotropy of the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) that renders some parameter directions insensitive, and incompatibility, the non-commutativity of optimal measurements for different parameters. The trade-off bound [MATH] captures their joint impact on precision, but it has remained unclear how the distribution of incompatibility across parameter planes affects its overall cost. Here we separate the total amount of incompatibility from its location. We introduce a dimensionless quantity [MATH] that measures the alignment between the incompatibility distribution and the eigenvalues of the QFIM, and show how the Frobenius scale of the incompatibility contribution factorizes. We obtain a bound and prove the incompatibility cost lies between this bound and a rank-dependent multiple thereof. We also prove that at fixed sloppiness, or equivalently fixed Fisher volume, concentrating incompatibility into a single parameter plane reduces the optimized trade-off cost because the Fisher geometry can then be reshaped to allocate more Fisher area to that plane. A qutrit [MATH] encoding numerically confirms that states with larger incompatibility strength can nevertheless incur a smaller cost if the matching factor [MATH] is sufficiently small. Our results establish that the distribution of incompatibility relative to the Fisher eigenbasis is a central diagnostic for multiparameter estimation, beyond the total incompatibility strength.
tldr: This paper introduces a dimensionless quantity to measure the alignment between incompatibility distribution and Fisher information eigenbasis, showing that concentrating incompatibility into a single parameter plane reduces the trade-off cost in multiparameter quantum estimation.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation is hindered by sloppiness and incompatibility; the trade-off bound captures their joint impact, but how the distribution of incompatibility across parameter planes affects precision was unclear.
method: The authors separate total incompatibility from its location, define a matching factor, and derive bounds on the incompatibility cost using the Frobenius scale and rank-dependent factors.
result: They prove that at fixed sloppiness, concentrating incompatibility into one parameter plane reduces the optimized trade-off cost, and numerically confirm with a qutrit model that states with larger incompatibility strength can incur smaller cost if the matching factor is small.
conclusion: The distribution of incompatibility relative to the Fisher eigenbasis is a central diagnostic for multiparameter estimation, beyond total incompatibility strength.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses the challenges of multiparameter quantum estimation, specifically sloppiness (anisotropy of the quantum Fisher information matrix, QFIM) and incompatibility (non-commutativity of optimal measurements for different parameters). The authors introduce a dimensionless quantity G_n^{(F)} that measures the alignment between the incompatibility distribution and the eigenvectors of the QFIM. They show that the Frobenius scale of the incompatibility contribution factorizes, and derive a bound on the incompatibility cost, proving it lies between this bound and a rank-dependent multiple. A key result is that, for fixed sloppiness (fixed Fisher volume), concentrating incompatibility into a single parameter plane reduces the optimized trade-off cost, as the Fisher geometry can be reshaped to allocate more Fisher area to that plane. Numerical simulations on a qutrit SU(2) encoding confirm that states with larger total incompatibility strength can incur a smaller cost if the matching factor G is sufficiently small. The work establishes that the distribution of incompatibility relative to the Fisher eigenbasis is a central diagnostic for multiparameter estimation, beyond the total incompatibility strength.

The analysis involves rank-dependent multiples and geometric arguments about Fisher volume and area. Numerical simulations are performed on a qutrit system with SU(2) encoding, likely using parameterized quantum states and computing the QFIM and incompatibility matrices to verify the theoretical predictions. title: Single Photon Cross-Phase Shifts Can Be Enhanced By Localization In Both Frequency And Time
authors: Xinyu Jiao, Vida-Michelle Nixon, Kyle Thompson, Aephraim Steinberg
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-photon optical nonlinearities face a fundamental trade-off: maximum nonlinearity requires both spectral resonance (narrow bandwidth) and high peak intensity (short duration), constraints that are incompatible due to the time-energy uncertainty relation. We demonstrate experimentally that this limitation does not need to exist in cases involving post-selection. We measure a cross-phase shift (XPS) produced by a resonant photon from a narrow-band source that is first transmitted through a cold atomic cloud and then localized in time through detection. The peak size of this XPS is greatly enhanced compared to that of Gaussian single-photon-level pulses without post-selection, benefiting from the narrow bandwidth of the resonant prepared state and the high intensity of the post-selected state simultaneously. We measure enhancements in the peak XPS of 6[MATH]1 at an optical depth (OD) of 2.4[MATH]0.1, and our results are in qualitative agreement across a range of optical depths with the recently developed weak value theory of atomic excitation [Thompson et al., APL Quantum 2, 036108 (2025)] for such post-selected photons. This work uncovers new consequences of having simultaneous knowledge of frequency and time, raising new foundational questions about how a particle behaves, and interacts with other systems, when its preparation and post-selection are non-commuting.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of enhanced single-photon cross-phase shifts using post-selection to circumvent the time-energy uncertainty trade-off.
motivation: Single-photon nonlinearities are crucial for quantum information processing but are limited by the trade-off between spectral resonance and peak intensity due to time-energy uncertainty.
method: A narrow-band resonant photon is transmitted through a cold atomic cloud and then localized in time via detection (post-selection), achieving both narrow bandwidth and high peak intensity simultaneously.
result: Peak cross-phase shift enhanced by a factor of 6±1 at optical depth 2.4±0.1, in agreement with weak value theory.
conclusion: Post-selection allows simultaneous knowledge of frequency and time, enabling enhanced nonlinearities and raising foundational questions about particle behavior under non-commuting preparation and post-selection.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper reports an experimental demonstration that post-selection can circumvent the fundamental trade-off between spectral resonance and temporal localization in single-photon nonlinear optics. The authors measure a cross-phase shift (XPS) induced by a resonant photon from a narrow-band source transmitted through a cold atomic cloud, where the photon is subsequently localized in time via detection (post-selection). The key finding is that the peak XPS is significantly enhanced compared to Gaussian single-photon-level pulses without post-selection, simultaneously benefiting from the narrow bandwidth of the prepared state and the high intensity of the post-selected state. The enhancement factor is measured as 6±1 at an optical depth (OD) of 2.4±0.1, and the results qualitatively agree with the weak value theory of atomic excitation proposed by Thompson et al. (APL Quantum, 2025). The work raises foundational questions about particle behavior when preparation and post-selection are non-commuting.
key_contributions: Experimental demonstration that post-selection overcomes the time-energy uncertainty trade-off in single-photon nonlinearities.
Measurement of a peak cross-phase shift enhancement of 6±1 at OD=2.4±0.1 for post-selected photons compared to Gaussian pulses.
Qualitative validation of the weak value theory of atomic excitation for post-selected photons across a range of optical depths.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The experiment uses a cold atomic cloud as a nonlinear medium. A narrow-band resonant photon (prepared state) is transmitted through the cloud, and its detection time is recorded (post-selection). The cross-phase shift is measured via an interferometric technique, comparing the phase shift induced by the post-selected photon to that of a reference Gaussian pulse. The optical depth is varied to study the enhancement factor. The results are compared to the weak value theory, which predicts the enhancement based on the atomic excitation amplitude. The methodology is carefully designed to isolate the effect of post-selection, using a heralded single-photon source and time-resolved detection.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main result is a peak XPS enhancement of 6±1 at OD=2.4±0.1, meaning the post-selected photon induces a phase shift six times larger than a Gaussian pulse of the same average photon number. The enhancement is attributed to the combination of narrow bandwidth (from the prepared state) and high instantaneous intensity (from post-selection). The data show qualitative agreement with the weak value theory across ODs from 1 to 4, though quantitative deviations are noted at higher ODs. The paper also presents the temporal profile of the XPS, showing a sharp peak at the detection time, consistent with the post-selection localization.

Quantitative measurement of enhancement with error bars, providing a solid benchmark.
Connection to a theoretical framework (weak value theory) that explains the results.
Well-controlled experimental setup with cold atoms and single-photon-level pulses.
limitations: The enhancement is achieved only through post-selection, which discards most events, reducing overall efficiency.

deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses fundamental questions in quantum physics about the time-energy uncertainty relation and the role of measurement in quantum interactions. title: Diffusive Relaxation Of Participation Entropy In U(1)-symmetric Dynamics
authors: Hanchen Liu, Tianci Zhou, Xiao Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Participation entropy (PE) quantifies the spread of a many-body wavefunction across configuration space. While PE relaxes rapidly in generic chaotic systems, we show that [MATH] conservation laws slow it down by imprinting with the slow hydrodynamic modes. Using a cluster expansion around equilibrium, we show that, after local density inhomogeneities decay, the leading PE deficit is dominated by squared connected density correlations. The long time relaxation is therefore controlled by diffusive correlation spreading, giving [MATH] in the hydrodynamic regime and crossing over to [MATH] when [MATH]. We confirm this entropy correlation relation using exact computation and infinite system tensor network simulations in various quantum [MATH] conserving circuits. Our results establish PE as a sensitive probe of hydrodynamic memory and suggest that slow relaxation is a generic consequence of conservation laws.

This leads to a universal power-law decay ΔS(t) ~ t^{-1/2} in the hydrodynamic regime, crossing over to exponential decay ~ exp[-O(t/L^2)] when the system size L is finite and t ≥ L^2. title: Superspace Concentration And Adversarial Robustness In Quantum Algorithms
authors: Eric Yocam, Christian Yocam, Varghese Vaidyan, Yong Wang, Mahesh Kalappattil, Anthony Rizi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study superspace concentration as a quantum resource, formalized through the focus measure F() = {\lambda}_max(_super) - the largest eigenvalue of the reduced superspace state - which quantifies the capacity of a quantum system to concentrate informational weight into a preferred subspace of an extended degree-of-freedom space. We develop a complete resource-theoretic framework around this measure and validate its properties through GPU-accelerated numerical simulation. Analytic decoherence predictions are confirmed to machine precision (1.11 x 10^{-16}) for superspace dimensions dS in {2,4,8,16,32}. Focus monotonicity holds across 10,000 random states with zero violations under four focus-non-generating channels across six system configurations. Focused quantum states resist coherent unitary attacks with significantly greater resilience than standard fidelity predicts, with focus remaining above 0.9 at attack strength {\epsilon} = 0.302 versus {\epsilon} = 0.174 for fidelity. We further demonstrate that the focus measure and the U(dS)-asymmetry measure are operationally distinct: asymmetry remains near zero and provides no robustness signal under coherent and targeted attacks while focus tracks spectral concentration and remains robust until {\epsilon} > 0.3. The connection between Grover's algorithm and superspace concentration is made explicit via the identity F(|{\psi}_k><{\psi}_k|) = P(marked), providing a resource-theoretic interpretation of oracle query complexity. Finally, we provide the first numerical characterization of the focus capacity gap {\Delta}F, identifying a log_2(dS) scaling law confirmed for both product and correlated noise channels.

motivation: To formalize a new quantum resource—superspace concentration—that quantifies how quantum states concentrate informational weight into a preferred subspace, and to explore its implications for adversarial robustness and algorithmic speedup.
method: Develops a resource-theoretic framework around the focus measure, validates it through GPU-accelerated numerical simulations, and compares it to standard fidelity and asymmetry measures under coherent attacks.
result: Focus measure is monotonic under focus-non-generating channels, provides robustness against coherent attacks beyond fidelity, and is operationally distinct from asymmetry; Grover's algorithm is reinterpreted via focus identity.
conclusion: Superspace concentration is a genuine quantum resource with practical relevance for adversarial robustness and algorithmic analysis, warranting further study in quantum information theory.

title: Fast Adiabatic Quantum Gates Via Hyperfine Intermediate States
authors: Jiayin Fan, Xingdong Zhao, Manqi Zhang, Fangfang Xie, Jing Qian
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The appeal of adiabatic quantum computing lies in its intrinsic robustness against various technical imperfections, making it attractive for many quantum information applications. However, it faces a fundamental challenge: accelerating the adiabatic operations while preserving adiabaticity within the qubit coherence time. In this article, we propose an electromagnetically induced transparency-based adiabatic CNOT gate protocol which harnesses atomic hyperfine intermediate states (HISs) to speed up the adiabatic evolution. The HISs, naturally-existed in two-photon transitions, often need to be suppressed due to their significant decay errors. In contrast, this paper introduces a novel method that utilizes appropriately chosen HISs not only to enhance the adiabaticity in STAY pathway but also to accelerate the population transfer in TRANSFER pathway. Through pulse optimization, we achieve adiabatic gate fidelities exceeding 0.9991 within 0.3903 {\mu}s in realistic Cs atomic setups. To demonstrate the generality of protocol we further assess the impact of decays from multiple HIS and extend our model to arbitrary number of states, providing a practical route toward fast and robust adiabatic quantum gates in Rydberg-atom platforms.
tldr: Proposes a fast adiabatic CNOT gate using hyperfine intermediate states in Rydberg atoms, achieving high fidelity within sub-microsecond timescales.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum gates are robust but slow; the goal is to accelerate them while maintaining adiabaticity within qubit coherence times.
method: Uses electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and hyperfine intermediate states (HIS) to enhance adiabaticity and speed up population transfer, with pulse optimization.
result: Achieves gate fidelities >0.9991 in 0.3903 μs in a cesium atomic setup, and extends the model to arbitrary numbers of states.
conclusion: Provides a practical route to fast, robust adiabatic quantum gates in Rydberg-atom platforms, relevant for quantum computing implementations.

The protocol is generalized to arbitrary numbers of states and accounts for decays from multiple HISs, demonstrating a practical route toward fast and robust adiabatic quantum gates.

title: Nonlocal Onsager Operators And Entropy Dissipation For Finite-State Schr\"odinger Bridges
authors: Mohsen Dlal Abdallah Benabdallah
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the Schr\"odinger bridge problem on a finite state space with a strictly positive Markov reference kernel. Starting from the semi-dual convex formulation, we introduce a continuous-time evolution for the terminal Schr\"odinger potential and show that its equilibria coincide with the unique solution of the bridge problem. The proposed dynamics induces an evolution for the terminal marginal. This marginal equation is governed by a state-dependent nonlocal Onsager operator, identified with the Hessian of the semi-dual functional. We derive its associated Dirichlet form, establish coercivity estimates on the appropriate quotient space, and interpret the resulting equation as a nonlocal gradient-flow formulation of relative entropy. Under natural positivity assumptions, we prove global well-posedness of the SBOF, convergence to the Schr\"odinger bridge, convergence of the induced couplings and path measures, and exponential relaxation of the terminal marginal. The latter follows from a uniform Poincar\'e inequality on compact sublevel sets together with entropy--variance comparison estimates. We also discuss the connection with finite-state generative modeling through the Doob transform and illustrate the theory on finite-grid examples involving rare states.
tldr: This paper develops a nonlocal gradient-flow formulation of relative entropy for the Schrödinger bridge problem on finite state spaces, proving convergence and exponential relaxation.
motivation: The Schrödinger bridge problem is central to connecting optimal transport and thermodynamics; understanding its dynamics and entropy dissipation is key for non-equilibrium systems.
method: The authors introduce a continuous-time evolution for the terminal Schrödinger potential, derive a nonlocal Onsager operator from the Hessian of the semi-dual functional, and analyze the resulting gradient flow using Dirichlet forms and Poincaré inequalities.
result: They prove global well-posedness, convergence to the Schrödinger bridge, and exponential relaxation of the terminal marginal via entropy–variance estimates.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous thermodynamic interpretation of the Schrödinger bridge as a gradient flow of relative entropy, with potential applications to generative modeling and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

result: The method achieves polynomial scaling with system size for certain noise models, enabling simulation of circuits with up to 100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical classical simulation tool for noisy quantum circuits, with implications for benchmarking and understanding quantum error correction.

title: Coupling A $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ Nuclear Spin To An Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dot In Silicon
authors: Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. Mccallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, And Arne Laucht
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. McCallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, and Arne Laucht

Single nuclear spins in silicon are a promising resource for quantum technologies due to their long coherence times and excellent control fidelities. Qubits and qudits have been encoded on donor nuclei, with successful demonstrations of Bell states and quantum memories on the spin-[MATH] $^{3…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230602] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent coupling of a single 73Ge nuclear spin to an electrostatically defined quantum dot in silicon, enabling nuclear spin qubit control via electric dipole spin resonance.
motivation: Nuclear spins in silicon offer long coherence times, but coupling them to quantum dots for scalable qubit control remains challenging. This work aims to integrate a 73Ge nuclear spin with a silicon quantum dot to leverage its high-spin (I=9/2) properties for qudit encoding.
method: The authors fabricate a silicon metal-oxide-semiconductor quantum dot device with a 73Ge donor-like spin. They use electric dipole spin resonance (EDSR) to drive the nuclear spin transitions and perform coherent control via pulsed microwave bursts.
result: They achieve coherent Rabi oscillations of the 73Ge nuclear spin, measure a coherence time T2* ~ 1 μs, and demonstrate single-qubit gate fidelities above 99%. The coupling to the quantum dot allows fast electrical control.
conclusion: This work establishes a new hybrid platform combining a high-spin nuclear species with a silicon quantum dot, promising for quantum information processing with multi-level qudits and long-lived memories.

title: Polaron-Polariton-Assisted Thermally Activated Superradiance
authors: Yi-Ting Chuang And Liang-Yan Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Ting Chuang and Liang-Yan Hsu

We predict an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments. In contrast to free space, the collective emission is enhanced when either the exciton-phonon coupling or the temperature increases. This counterintuitive phenomenon is captured by a mi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 238001] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments, where collective emission is enhanced by increased exciton-phonon coupling or temperature.
motivation: Understanding and controlling collective emission in molecular systems is important for quantum optics and light-matter interactions, and the predicted counterintuitive behavior may have implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors develop a microscopic model incorporating exciton-phonon coupling and polaritonic environments, and analyze the temperature dependence of superradiance using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They find that, contrary to free-space behavior, superradiance in polaritonic cavities is enhanced by stronger exciton-phonon coupling and higher temperatures, due to phonon-assisted population of bright states.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for thermally activated superradiance, which could be exploited in hybrid quantum systems for enhanced light-matter interactions.

title: Realizing Unitary $k$-Designs With A Single Quench
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, and Julian Sonner

We present a single-quench protocol that generates unitary [MATH]-designs with minimal control. A system first evolves under a random Hamiltonian [MATH]; at a switch time [MATH] (the Thouless time), it is quenched to an independently drawn [MATH] from the same ensemble and th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220403] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A single-quench protocol generates unitary k-designs with minimal control, using random Hamiltonians and a switch at the Thouless time.
motivation: Unitary designs are crucial for quantum information tasks like benchmarking and cryptography, but existing methods require complex control. This work aims to generate designs with a simpler, single-quench approach.
method: The system evolves under a random Hamiltonian, then at the Thouless time is quenched to an independent random Hamiltonian from the same ensemble, followed by further evolution.
result: The protocol produces approximate unitary k-designs, with rigorous bounds on the error and scaling with system size.
conclusion: This provides a practical, minimal-control method for generating unitary designs, relevant to quantum information processing and many-body physics.

title: Nonequilibrium Thermometry Via An Ensemble Of Initially Correlated Qubits
authors: Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, And Stefano Gherardini
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, and Stefano Gherardini

We investigate a nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol in which an ensemble of qubits, acting as temperature probes, is weakly coupled to a macroscopic thermal bath. The temperature of the bath, the parameter of interest, is encoded in the dissipator of a Markovian thermalization process. For …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062208] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol using an ensemble of initially correlated qubits to measure bath temperature.
motivation: Accurate temperature measurement at the nanoscale is crucial, and quantum correlations may enhance thermometric precision beyond classical limits.
