[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214426] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure and magnetism of kagome metals using ARPES and XMCD, focusing on band hybridization and induced Ti magnetism.
motivation: Kagome materials host emergent quantum phenomena, and understanding their electronic and magnetic properties is crucial for advancing condensed matter physics.
method: The authors combine angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), density functional theory (DFT), and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) to investigate the kagome metals R Ti3 Bi4 (R = Nd, Sm, Gd).
result: They observe hybridized kagome bands and induced Ti magnetism, providing detailed electronic structure and magnetic characterization.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of kagome metals but do not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Entropic Clustering Of Stickers Induces Aging In Biocondensates
authors: Hugo Le Roy And Paolo de Los Rios
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Le Roy and Paolo De Los Rios

Biomolecular condensates are cellular phase-separated droplets that usually exhibit a viscoelastic mechanical response, a behavior rationalized by modeling the complex molecules that make up a condensate as stickers and spacers, which assemble into a network-like structure. Condensates usually exhib…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064405] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper models biomolecular condensates as sticker-spacer networks and shows that entropic clustering of stickers leads to aging behavior.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates exhibit viscoelastic mechanical response, which is not fully understood. The authors aim to explain aging in these condensates using a minimal model.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on stickers and spacers, using statistical mechanics to study the dynamics of network formation and aging.
result: Entropic clustering of stickers leads to a gradual increase in network connectivity over time, resulting in aging behavior consistent with experimental observations.
conclusion: The sticker-spacer model with entropic clustering provides a mechanism for aging in biomolecular condensates, linking microscopic dynamics to macroscopic rheology.

title: Biased Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time Distributions As A Model Of Anomalous Diffusion In The Presence Of Drift
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, and Ralf Metzler

Mathematical models of diffusion based on stochastic processes of the type of continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are widely used for the description of various transport characteristics in complex media. An external or internal bias in a given CTRW model is often attributed to an asymmetric distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper models anomalous diffusion with drift using biased continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time distributions.
motivation: To understand transport in complex media where standard diffusion models fail, especially under external bias.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of CTRW with asymmetric waiting-time distributions and drift.
result: Derived expressions for mean squared displacement and other transport characteristics showing anomalous diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The model captures a range of anomalous diffusion behaviors in the presence of drift, relevant to biological and soft matter systems.

title: Exchange Monte Carlo For Continuous-space Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation
authors: Xun Zhao And Synge Todo
abstract:
Author(s): Xun Zhao and Synge Todo

We present an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) method designed for application in continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations at finite temperature. Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, particularly when measuring observables affected by pa…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exchange Monte Carlo method for continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo simulations to reduce autocorrelation times.
motivation: Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, especially for observables affected by permutation sampling.
method: The authors propose an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) algorithm that swaps configurations between different temperature replicas to improve sampling efficiency in continuous-space PIMC.
result: The EMC method reduces autocorrelation times and improves the accuracy of measured observables in bosonic systems.
conclusion: The proposed EMC technique is an effective tool for accelerating PIMC simulations of quantum many-body systems at finite temperature.

title: Further Testing The Validity Of Generalized Heterogeneous-elasticity Theory For Low-frequency Excitations In Structural Glasses
authors: Walter Schirmacher, Matteo Paoluzzi, Felix Cosmin Mocanu, Dmytro Khomenko, Grzegorz Szamel, Francesco Zamponi, And Giancarlo Ruocco

tldr: This paper tests the validity of generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory for low-frequency excitations in structural glasses, focusing on non-universal scaling of the vibrational density of states.
motivation: Understanding low-frequency excitations in glasses is important for their mechanical and thermal properties, but the universality of scaling laws is debated.
method: The authors summarize their previous theory and provide further computational evidence by analyzing vibrational modes in model glasses.
result: They demonstrate non-universality of the ω^4 scaling of the nonphononic vibrational density of states.
conclusion: Generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory captures the non-universal features, but the results are specific to structural glasses and not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Diffusion-driven Pattern Formation In An Opinion Dynamical Network Model
authors: Tim Mauch And Thilo Gross
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Mauch and Thilo Gross

The spatial organization of individuals and their interactions in communities are important factors known to preserve diversity in many complex systems. Inspired by metapopulation models from ecology, we study opinion formation using a network-based approach in which nodes represent communities of i…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion formation using a network-based metapopulation model, focusing on spatial pattern formation and diversity preservation.
motivation: Understanding how spatial organization and network structure influence opinion diversity in complex social systems.
method: A network model where nodes represent communities of individuals, with diffusion-driven dynamics inspired by ecological metapopulation models.
result: The model exhibits pattern formation and can maintain opinion diversity under certain conditions.
conclusion: Spatial structure and network topology are key factors in preserving diversity in opinion dynamics.

title: Free-energy Model Of Ferroelectric Transition In P(VDF-TrFE) Copolymer
authors: Vadim V. Atrazhev, Dmitry V. Dmitriev, And Vadim I. Sultanov
abstract:
Author(s): Vadim V. Atrazhev, Dmitry V. Dmitriev, and Vadim I. Sultanov

We develop a physics-based analytical model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in poly(vinylidene difluoride-co-trifluoroethylene) [P(VDF-TrFE)] copolymers. The low-temperature ferroelectric phase is an orthorhombic crystal analogous to the poly(vinylidene difluoride) β-phase, wh…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065405] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Develops a physics-based analytical model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers.
motivation: To understand the phase transition mechanism in a technologically relevant ferroelectric polymer.
method: Constructs a free-energy model based on the Landau-Devonshire theory, incorporating dipole interactions and chain conformations.
result: The model reproduces the temperature dependence of polarization and dielectric constant, and predicts the transition temperature as a function of copolymer composition.
conclusion: The analytical model provides a quantitative description of the ferroelectric transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers, useful for material design.

title: Virtual Cathode Behavior In A Crossed-field Gap
authors: Ashmita Panda, Jim Browning, And Allen L. Garner
abstract:
Author(s): Ashmita Panda, Jim Browning, and Allen L. Garner

While the behavior of virtual cathodes (VCs) in a space-charge limited gap in the absence of a magnetic field is well understood, it is less characterized for crossed-field gaps with perpendicular magnetic and electric fields. Thus, this study examines VC formation at steady state in a crossed-field…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065202] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies virtual cathode formation in crossed-field gaps, a topic in plasma physics and vacuum electronics.
motivation: Understanding virtual cathode behavior in crossed-field gaps is important for high-power microwave devices and vacuum electronics.
method: The authors use steady-state analysis and simulations to examine virtual cathode formation under perpendicular electric and magnetic fields.
result: They characterize the conditions for virtual cathode formation and its properties in crossed-field gaps.
conclusion: The study extends the understanding of virtual cathodes to crossed-field configurations, relevant for device design.

title: Externally Driven Condensates Show Translation-induced Polarization, Directed Coalescence, And Anomalous Diffusion In Viscoelastic Media
authors: Andriy Goychuk
abstract:
Author(s): Andriy Goychuk

Phase separation into compositionally and physically distinct domains is ubiquitous in (non)living matter ranging from alloys and emulsions to biomolecular condensates in cells. The organization of these domains can be controlled, for example, by nonequilibrium chemical reactions, external fields, o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065402] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase separation in viscoelastic media under external driving, focusing on polarization, coalescence, and anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Understanding how external fields and viscoelasticity control the organization of phase-separated domains in soft matter and biological systems.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of externally driven condensates in viscoelastic media.
result: Translation-induced polarization, directed coalescence, and anomalous diffusion are observed.
conclusion: External driving can be used to control domain organization in viscoelastic environments.

title: First-passage-time Properties Of Diffusion With A Broad Class Of Stochastic Diffusion Coefficients
authors: Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, And Hitoshi Washizu
abstract:
Author(s): Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, and Hitoshi Washizu

This study investigates the first-passage-time (FPT) properties of particles with a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients (DCs), representing diffusion in heterogeneous environments or of particles with conformational fluctuations. We demonstrate that for diffusion in a one-dimen…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064108] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage-time properties of diffusion with stochastic diffusion coefficients in heterogeneous environments.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in heterogeneous media is important for transport in disordered systems and biological processes.
method: Analytical and numerical methods are used to derive FPT distributions for a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients in one dimension.
result: The paper characterizes how stochastic diffusion coefficients affect the first-passage-time statistics, revealing universal scaling behaviors.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into diffusion in complex environments but have no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Relative-advection-induced Instability In A Reaction-diffusion-advection System
authors: Chuanjun Dai, Ruyi Zhou, Qing Guo, And Min Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Chuanjun Dai, Ruyi Zhou, Qing Guo, and Min Zhao

The instability mechanism in general reaction-diffusion-advection systems is key to understanding flow-driven self-organization. Here we report the general conditions for instability in [MATH]-dimensional space, formally termed relative advection instability (RAI) given its exclusive dependence on the …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064202] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies instability in reaction-diffusion-advection systems, a topic in nonlinear dynamics and pattern formation.
motivation: Understanding flow-driven self-organization in reaction-diffusion-advection systems is important for biological and chemical pattern formation.
method: The authors derive general conditions for instability in n-dimensional space, termed relative advection instability (RAI), using linear stability analysis.
result: They identify conditions under which advection induces instability, independent of diffusion-driven Turing instability.
conclusion: RAI provides a new mechanism for pattern formation in advective systems, with potential applications in ecology and fluid dynamics.

title: Resetting-induced Instability In Queues Fed By A Search Process In An Interval
authors: José Giral-Barajas And Paul C. Bressloff
abstract:
Author(s): José Giral-Barajas and Paul C. Bressloff

Proper management of resources whose arrival and consumption are subject to environmental randomness is an intrinsic process in both natural and artificial systems. This phenomenon can be modeled as a queuing process whose arrival distribution is determined by a search process with stochastic resett…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064101] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a queuing model where arrivals are governed by a search process with stochastic resetting, leading to instability.
motivation: To understand how resetting in search processes affects the stability of queues, which is relevant to resource management in random environments.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a queue fed by a search process on an interval with resetting, deriving conditions for instability.
result: Resetting can induce instability in the queue even when the underlying search process would otherwise be stable.
conclusion: Stochastic resetting can fundamentally alter queue dynamics, with implications for natural and artificial systems.

title: Unveiling Dielectric Relaxation And Shear Rheology In Water
authors: Songming Liu And Jiaxing Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Songming Liu and Jiaxing Yuan

The complex dynamics of liquid water are manifested in its unique dielectric relaxation and nonlinear shear rheology. We investigate the dielectric and rheological responses of TIP4P/[MATH] water using molecular dynamics simulations across a wide temperature range, including the deeply supercooled regi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023266] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics study of dielectric relaxation and shear rheology in water using TIP4P model.
motivation: Understanding the complex dynamics of liquid water, especially in the supercooled regime, is important for fundamental physics and applications.
method: Classical molecular dynamics simulations of TIP4P water across a wide temperature range, analyzing dielectric and rheological responses.
result: The paper reports temperature-dependent dielectric relaxation times and nonlinear shear rheology behavior.
conclusion: The study provides insights into water's dynamical properties but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamic Similarity Of Vortex Shedding In A Superfluid Flowing Past A Penetrable Obstacle
authors: Junhwan Kwon And Yong-Il Shin
abstract:
Author(s): Junhwan Kwon and Yong-il Shin

We numerically investigate wake dynamics in a superfluid flowing past a penetrable obstacle. The penetrable obstacle does not fully deplete the density, and we define an effective diameter [MATH] from the Mach-1 contour of the time-averaged irrotational flow around the obstacle, which …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023246] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of vortex shedding dynamics in a superfluid flowing past a penetrable obstacle, focusing on dynamic similarity and effective diameter definition.
motivation: To understand wake dynamics in superfluids with penetrable obstacles, which are relevant to quantum turbulence and superfluid hydrodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a superfluid flow past a penetrable obstacle, analyzing vortex shedding patterns and defining an effective diameter from the Mach-1 contour.
result: The vortex shedding frequency scales with the effective diameter, showing dynamic similarity analogous to classical fluids.
conclusion: Penetrable obstacles in superfluids exhibit vortex shedding with dynamic similarity, extending classical fluid dynamics concepts to quantum fluids.

title: Reducibility Of Higher-order To Pairwise Interactions: Social Impact Models On Hypergraphs
authors: Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, And Federico Vázquez
abstract:
Author(s): Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, and Federico Vázquez

We show that a general class of node-update social impact models with higher-order interactions on hypergraphs can be exactly mapped to an equivalent model with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network. This mapping preserves the microscopic probabilities of changing the state of the no…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023250] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that higher-order social impact models on hypergraphs can be reduced to pairwise interactions on weighted projected networks.
motivation: To simplify the analysis of complex social systems with higher-order interactions by mapping them to well-understood pairwise models.
method: The authors derive an exact mathematical mapping from a class of node-update social impact models on hypergraphs to equivalent models with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network.
result: The mapping preserves microscopic state-change probabilities, enabling the use of pairwise network tools for hypergraph models.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions in social impact models can be effectively captured by pairwise interactions with appropriate weights, simplifying theoretical and computational analysis.

title: Compression, Simulation, And Synthesis Of Turbulent Flows With Tensor Trains
authors: Stefano Pisoni, Raghavendra D. Peddinti, Siddhartha E. Guzman, Egor Tiunov, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Pisoni, Raghavendra D. Peddinti, Siddhartha E. Guzman, Egor Tiunov, and Leandro Aolita

Numerical simulations of turbulent fluids are paramount to real-life applications, from predicting and modeling flows to diagnostic purposes in engineering. However, they are also computationally challenging due to their intrinsically nonlinear dynamics, which require a very high spatial resolution …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023245] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies tensor train decompositions to compress, simulate, and synthesize turbulent fluid flows, focusing on computational efficiency for classical fluid dynamics.
motivation: Turbulent flow simulations are computationally expensive due to high spatial resolution requirements; tensor methods offer a way to reduce complexity.
method: The authors use tensor train (TT) decompositions to represent turbulent flow data and dynamics, enabling compression and efficient simulation.
result: The TT-based approach achieves significant compression ratios and accelerates simulations while maintaining accuracy for certain turbulent flow regimes.
conclusion: Tensor train methods are a promising tool for classical fluid dynamics, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Phenomenology Of Orbital Torque, Pumping, And Mixing Conductance In Metallic Bilayers
authors: Xiaobai Ning, Henri Jaffrès, Weisheng Zhao, And Aurélien Manchon
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaobai Ning, Henri Jaffrès, Weisheng Zhao, and Aurélien Manchon

The conversion between spin and orbital currents is at the origin of the orbital torque and its Onsager reciprocal, the orbital pumping. Here, we propose a phenomenological model to describe the orbital torque in magnetic bilayers composed of an orbital source (i.e., a light metal such as Ti, Ru, ${…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023239] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a phenomenological model for orbital torque and pumping in metallic bilayers, focusing on spin-orbit conversion in light metals.
motivation: Understanding orbital-to-spin current conversion is important for spintronic devices, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a phenomenological model based on spin diffusion and orbital diffusion equations to describe orbital torque and pumping in magnetic bilayers.
result: They derive expressions for orbital torque, pumping, and mixing conductance, and discuss the role of orbital Hall effect and orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect.
conclusion: The model provides a framework for interpreting experiments on orbital torque, but the work is purely within condensed matter spintronics without quantum information or thermodynamic implications.

title: From Knots To Crystals: Machine-learned Potentials For Self-assembling Topological Solitons In Liquid Crystals
authors: Arunkumar Bupathy, Darian Hall, Ivan I. Smalyukh, Gerardo Campos-Villalobos, Rodolfo Subert, And Marjolein Dijkstra
abstract:
Author(s): Arunkumar Bupathy, Darian Hall, Ivan I. Smalyukh, Gerardo Campos-Villalobos, Rodolfo Subert, and Marjolein Dijkstra

Knotted fields in classical and quantum systems have long been recognized for their nontrivial topologies and particlelike behavior, but practical applications have been limited by the difficulty of stabilizing them. Recently, stable knotted solitonic textures—heliknotons—were discovered in chiral l…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023235] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Uses machine-learned potentials to study self-assembly of topological solitons (heliknotons) in liquid crystals.
motivation: Stable knotted solitonic textures in liquid crystals have potential applications but are difficult to stabilize and control; the paper aims to predict their self-assembly into ordered phases.
method: Develops machine-learned interaction potentials from simulation data and uses them in coarse-grained simulations to study the phase behavior of heliknotons.
result: Identifies conditions under which heliknotons self-assemble into crystalline and other ordered phases, and characterizes the resulting structures.
conclusion: Machine-learned potentials enable efficient exploration of self-assembly in topological soliton systems, opening avenues for designing novel materials.

authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting devices, which is important for superconducting electronics.
method: The authors use local protonic gating in homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect without breaking time-reversal symmetry.
result: They observe a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents with zero applied magnetic field.
conclusion: This work provides a new mechanism for superconducting diodes that could be useful for low-power electronics and quantum devices.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of a uniform ferro-rotational order in Ni2Mo3O8 that intertwines polar and chiral orders, forming complex domain walls.
motivation: To understand the interplay between multiple ferroic orders (polar, chiral, ferro-rotational) in a single material and explore the resulting domain wall physics.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were used to identify and map the ferro-rotational order and its coupling to polarity and chirality.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state is identified, which couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of multiferroic order and highlight the potential for domain wall engineering in homo-ferro-rotational insulators.
