[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of buckling instabilities in growing soft matter using nonlinear elasticity theory.
motivation: To understand the formation of wrinkles, creases, and cusps in soft materials under compression or growth, which is relevant to materials science and biology.
method: Integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.
result: Provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and the nonlinear phenomena accompanying buckling.
conclusion: Nonlinear elasticity theory is essential for a complete understanding of creases and sharp cusps in growing soft matter.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of using gravitational waves to probe the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can reveal the first second of the universe, which is opaque to light and neutrinos.
method: Review of theoretical signals from cosmological sources and detection strategies for stochastic gravitational waves.
result: Summarizes possible gravitational wave signals from early universe events and outlines detection methods.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique window into the early universe, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools for constructing and using Wannier functions in electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper reviews the theoretical background of Wannier functions and describes the software ecosystem including Wannier90 and related codes.
result: It highlights the wide range of applications from accurate integrations to topological invariants.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community.

title: Electric-field-driven Nanoconfinement And The 5–120 Nm Stability Regime Of Piezoelectric Β-glycine
authors: Kexin Zhang And Zhengbao Yang
abstract: Piezoelectric β-glycine is a promising molecular crystal, yet its controlled preparation remains challenging. Current nanoconfinement strategies, which rely primarily on rigid templates or simulations, cannot reliably capture the intrinsic confinement regime that leads to β-phase formation. Here, we propose electric-field-driven nanoconfinement as a one-step, continuous, and interface-free approach to investigate glycine crystallization and to define the confinement regime that yields the β-phase. We produced glycine nanoparticles via electrohydrodynamic spraying under a direct current field, automatically varying the spraying height to modulate nanoconfinement during nucleation and growth. Structural, morphological, and piezoelectric characterizations reveal that pure β-glycine forms within a crystal radius range of 5–120 nm. By integrating these findings with thermodynamic and kinetic analysis, we elucidate the mechanism of β-phase formation and construct a crystallization phase map that delineates the confinement conditions necessary for its stabilization. This work identifies the critical nanoconfinement parameters for accessing piezoelectric β-glycine and provides fundamental insights into polymorph control in molecular crystalline materials.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field-driven nanoconfinement to stabilize piezoelectric β-glycine, a molecular crystal, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Controlled preparation of piezoelectric β-glycine is challenging; current nanoconfinement methods cannot reliably capture the intrinsic confinement regime for β-phase formation.
method: Electric-field-driven nanoconfinement via electrohydrodynamic spraying under DC field, varying spraying height to modulate confinement during nucleation and growth.
result: Pure β-glycine forms within a crystal radius range of 5–120 nm; a crystallization phase map delineating confinement conditions is constructed.
conclusion: The work identifies critical nanoconfinement parameters for accessing piezoelectric β-glycine and provides insights into polymorph control in molecular crystals.

title: The Era Of Extremely Large Optical Telescopes Ii: The Gmt And Tmt
authors: Priya Hasan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The advent of Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs) ground-based optical and infrared observatories with primary mirrors exceeding 20m marks a transformative era in observational astronomy. This article explores the dawn of this new age, focusing on two of the next generation of optical/ infrared facilities: the Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) and the Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) We describe the key technological innovations enabling the construction of these ambitious observatories, notably, segmented mirror design, advanced adaptive optics (AO), and laser guide star systems. Collectively, these breakthroughs yield more than an order of magnitude increase in both light-gathering area and spatial resolution, delivering image sharpness that, for widefield observations, surpassing space-based telescopes. We shall also discuss the comparison of space and ground-based telescopes and highlight their individual strengths and why space telescopes are not the solution to the satellite interference to ground-based telescopes. Ground based telescopes will continue to always be leaders in astronomical observations.
tldr: This paper reviews the design and technology of the Giant Magellan Telescope and Thirty Meter Telescope, two upcoming extremely large optical telescopes.
motivation: To describe the technological innovations enabling the construction of next-generation ground-based optical telescopes with mirrors over 20 meters.
method: The paper provides a descriptive overview of segmented mirror design, adaptive optics, and laser guide star systems used in GMT and TMT.
result: These telescopes will offer more than an order of magnitude increase in light-gathering area and spatial resolution, surpassing space-based telescopes for wide-field observations.
conclusion: Ground-based extremely large telescopes will continue to lead astronomical observations despite satellite interference.

title: Pulse-Duration Scaling Of Ultrafast Laser-Induced Damage Threshold In Hybrid Gratings
authors: Enam Chowdhury Ziyao Su
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High damage threshold gratings are in demand worldwide as critical components for next generation ultrahigh intensity lasers. Here we investigate the pulse-duration dependence of ultrafast laser-induced damage thresholds (LIDT) in hybrid multilayer dielectric gratings, touted to combine superior performance properties of both metallic and multilayer dielectric (MLD) gratings, using a dynamic finite-difference time-domain model incorporated with linear and non-linear absorption models. Simulations agree with reported experimental LIDT values for three representative designs and predict scaling exponents which vary with pulse durations ranging from 10 to 500 fs. The results reveal strong dependence on both material bandgap and grating field distribution, providing guidance for designing high LIDT gratings.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast laser-induced damage thresholds in hybrid multilayer dielectric gratings using simulations.
motivation: High damage threshold gratings are needed for next-generation ultrahigh intensity lasers.
method: A dynamic finite-difference time-domain model with linear and nonlinear absorption models is used to simulate damage thresholds.
result: Simulations match experimental values and show scaling exponents depend on pulse duration, material bandgap, and field distribution.
conclusion: The results provide guidance for designing high LIDT gratings.

title: From Rings To Top-Hat Beams
authors: M. A. J\'acome-Silva, I. Jul\'ian-Mac\'ias, I. Ramos-Prieto, U. Ru\'iz-Corona, F. Soto-Eguibar, D. S\'anchez-De-La-Llave, H. M. Moya-Cessa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the exact analytical paraxial propagation of structured light beams that transition from Ring annular profiles to top-hat intensity distributions. The initial field is defined as a superposition of a Gaussian-weighted power-law core and a singular inverse-quadratic modulation term, both carrying an azimuthal phase factor. By solving the Fresnel diffraction integral in cylindrical coordinates, we obtain exact closed-form expressions for the propagated field at arbitrary planes. The paraxial evolution is shown to be governed by a Cauchy-Riemann beam term and an infinite series of modified Bessel functions of the second kind weighted by an azimuthal phase factor. This analytical framework demonstrates how tuning the source parameters enables a continuous transition from ring-dominated annular profiles to uniform top-hat beams. For the fundamental mode ([MATH]), the singular component fills the central intensity null, producing a flat transverse plateau.
tldr: This paper presents an analytical solution for paraxial propagation of structured light beams transitioning from ring to top-hat profiles.
motivation: To provide exact closed-form expressions for beam propagation that enable continuous shaping of annular to uniform intensity distributions.
method: Solves the Fresnel diffraction integral in cylindrical coordinates for an initial field composed of a Gaussian-weighted power-law core and a singular inverse-quadratic modulation with azimuthal phase.
result: Obtains exact expressions involving a Cauchy-Riemann beam term and infinite series of modified Bessel functions, demonstrating tunable transition from ring to top-hat beams.
conclusion: The analytical framework allows precise control over beam profiles, with potential applications in optical trapping and laser material processing.

title: A Stochastic Model For Elastoplastic Contact Of Rough Surfaces Incorporating Scale-dependent Hardness
authors: Yang Xu, Hengxu Song, Jianqiao Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stress concentrations caused by inherent roughness of natural and manufactured surfaces often induce plastic deformation at contact interfaces, a challenge compounded by competing influences of the size effect of plastic deformation and self-affine rough surface topography. To address this, we developed a novel methodology based on stochastic theory using compounded Chapman-Kolmogorov equations, for the first time, to solve elastoplastic contact problems involving scale-dependent hardness. Our approach formulates three integral equations describing the evolution of probability density functions of elastic contact pressure, relative plastic contact area, and relative non-contact area across geometrical scales. We thoroughly investigate the effects of scale-dependent hardness on contact pressure distribution, relative elastic and plastic contact areas, and the area-to-load relationship. By adjusting various mechanical and material properties, our model predicts a smooth transition from linear elasticity to elastic-plastic behavior and finally to full plasticity. A key advancement is the derivation of a new topographic yield parameter incorporating a wider range of material and geometrical properties, aiding identification of contact status. Numerical solutions enable highly precise determination of elastic and plastic limits via curve-fitting, and we also provide a new diagram for rapid identification of contact status. This study pioneers a stochastic process framework for applying the compounded Chapman-Kolmogorov equation to rough surface contact analysis, and the integral equations characterizing how interfacial properties evolve with scale could offer valuable insights for other multidisciplinary fields where multiscale roughness is critical, such as earthquakes, electrical contact, and contact electrification.
tldr: This paper develops a stochastic model for elastoplastic contact of rough surfaces with scale-dependent hardness using Chapman-Kolmogorov equations.
motivation: Rough surface contact induces plastic deformation, and existing models do not account for scale-dependent hardness and self-affine topography simultaneously.
method: The authors formulate three integral equations for probability density functions of elastic contact pressure, relative plastic contact area, and relative non-contact area across scales, solved numerically.
result: The model predicts a smooth transition from elasticity to plasticity, and a new topographic yield parameter is derived to identify contact status.
conclusion: This work provides a stochastic framework for rough surface contact analysis, with potential applications in tribology, earthquakes, and electrical contact.

title: The Geometry Of Admissible Short Selling In Discrete-Time Stochastic Portfolio Theory
authors: Xiaojun Cui Jilong Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While discrete-time Stochastic Portfolio Theory (SPT) provides a robust framework for market analysis, existing work on functional generation has predominantly focused on long-only portfolios defined on the entire unit simplex. This paper extends the geometric framework of functional generation to the broader class of bankruptcy-proof long-short portfolios defined on local market state spaces. We establish that, within this admissible setting, pseudo-arbitrage is fully characterized by the concavity of the generating function on the market state space, thereby relaxing the usual global domain requirement. A central contribution of this work is a geometric characterization of the short-selling mechanism. We prove that the presence of short selling is equivalent to the negativity of the maximal concave extension of the generating potential. This phenomenon is linked to the steepness of the logarithmic gradient as the market approaches a zero boundary nested inside the simplex. To systematically exploit this mechanism, we introduce the barycentric scaling transformation, a constructive methodology that maps classical long-only generating functions onto restricted domains to engineer admissible strategies with controlled short-selling exposure. Finally, through the analysis of specific shrunken portfolios, we identify a geometric phase transition: under suitable boundary conditions, admissible strategies exhibit a long-only core and a short-selling region in a qualitative sense (without asserting an exact partition of the state space). This provides a unified geometric perspective on relative arbitrage beyond the long-only constraint.
tldr: This paper extends stochastic portfolio theory to long-short portfolios with geometric characterizations of short selling and pseudo-arbitrage.
motivation: Existing work on functional generation in stochastic portfolio theory focuses on long-only portfolios; this paper aims to generalize to bankruptcy-proof long-short portfolios.
method: The authors develop a geometric framework using local market state spaces, introduce the barycentric scaling transformation, and analyze concave extensions of generating functions.
result: They prove that pseudo-arbitrage is characterized by concavity of the generating function, and short selling corresponds to negativity of the maximal concave extension. A geometric phase transition between long-only and short-selling regions is identified.
conclusion: The work provides a unified geometric perspective on relative arbitrage beyond the long-only constraint, but is purely in mathematical finance with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum hardware.

title: A Scalable Approach For Transient Thermal Modeling Of Automotive Power Electronics
authors: Neelakantan Padmanabhan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient thermal management is critical for the reliability and performance of power electronics systems in automotive applications. This work presents a computationally efficient modeling approach for transient thermal simulation of power electronic systems, with a focus on inverter modules using multiple MOSFETs mounted on a printed circuit board assembly (PCBA). A case study of an inverter module comprising six MOSFETs arranged as high-side and low-side pairs for a three phases system mounted on a PCBA, attached to a heat sink is considered. Computational fluid dynamic (CFD) simulations in Ansys Icepak are performed considering different heat transfer mechanisms, including natural convection, forced convection at constant velocity, and forced convection with varying flow velocity. A transient thermal model is developed using the Lumped Parameter Linear Superposition (LPLSP) method, a hybrid approach that combines lumped parameter modeling with the principle of linear superposition to capture transient thermal behavior efficiently. Temperatures of the components from the simulations are compared with temperatures from the LPLSP model and temperatures from a Linear Time Invariant (LTI) based reduced order model (ROM) developed for this system. It is observed that the LPLSP model is able to model a wide range of use cases very accurately with error of less than 5 %. This method enables rapid thermal performance evaluation of power electronics systems that have very fast transients in component level power dissipation and variations in ambient conditions, making it particularly well-suited for early-stage design iterations and long-duration mission profile simulations. The approach offers a practical path to reducing development cycles for automotive power electronics design.
tldr: This paper presents a lumped parameter linear superposition method for transient thermal modeling of automotive power electronics, focusing on inverter modules with MOSFETs.
motivation: Efficient thermal management is critical for reliability and performance of power electronics in automotive applications, and existing CFD simulations are computationally expensive for early-stage design iterations.
method: The authors develop a hybrid Lumped Parameter Linear Superposition (LPLSP) model that combines lumped parameter modeling with linear superposition, and compare it with CFD simulations and an LTI-based reduced order model.
result: The LPLSP model achieves less than 5% error across a wide range of use cases, including natural and forced convection with varying flow velocity.
conclusion: The LPLSP method enables rapid thermal performance evaluation for power electronics with fast transients, suitable for early-stage design and long-duration mission profiles.

title: Nineteen To The Dozen: Embedding The Neo-Riemannian Tonnetz Into A Cyclic 19_3 Symmetric Configuration
authors: Pawel Nurowski
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper bridges combinatorial geometry and music theory to solve the fundamental challenge of embedding classical Western harmony into the microtonal 19-tone equal temperament (19-TET). Inspired by Roger Penrose's observations on the mathematical elegance of 19-TET, we provide the theoretical foundation for a physical 19-TET acoustic piano currently under construction. However, playing classical 12-TET music on such an instrument poses a topological problem: emvedding the classical Euler-Riemann Tonnetz into the 19-TET universe inevitably distorts structural chords, creating dissonant ``wolves.'' By formalizing these harmonic spaces as incidence configurations (the 12_3 and 19_3 graphs) and utilizing integer cuts in our optimization model, we exhaustively prove that exactly 32 out of 36 Neo-Riemannian harmonic connections can be preserved. We demonstrate a strict 5-fold degeneracy of this optimum: there exist exactly 5 mathematically equivalent local packings for the wolf chords. Among these, we identify a unique canonical realization in which the 14 excised vertices form a perfectly contiguous geometric void along the primary Hamiltonian cycle. We reveal that the 4 inevitably broken edges represent the exact topological scars of the historical enharmonic diesis, and we formulate the Vicentino Hypothesis regarding 16th-century microtonal composition. Finally, to make this theoretical geometry physically playable, we design a novel 19-TET split-key keyboard, formalized through a biomechanical cost function that optimizes the performer's hand span. This work provides the complete theoretical, historical, and ergonomic blueprint for the next generation of microtonal acoustic instruments.
tldr: This paper bridges combinatorial geometry and music theory to embed classical harmony into 19-tone equal temperament, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To solve the topological problem of playing 12-TET music on a 19-TET piano by embedding the Tonnetz into a 19_3 symmetric configuration.
method: Formalizes harmonic spaces as incidence configurations and uses integer cuts in an optimization model to exhaustively prove preservation of Neo-Riemannian connections.
result: Exactly 32 out of 36 harmonic connections can be preserved, with a 5-fold degeneracy and a unique canonical realization; 4 broken edges correspond to the enharmonic diesis.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical, historical, and ergonomic blueprint for a 19-TET acoustic piano with a split-key keyboard.

title: Does 2026 Ai Exhibit Intelligence, Or Can Claude Outsmart Pierre Or Catherine ?
authors: Robert C. Dalang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a sequence of high-school level mathematics questions that were not available on the Internet, we compare the performance of the popular AI software Claude with that of my friends and fellow human beings Pierre and Catherine. Pierre had solid scientific training as a young man, while Catherine studied literature. All three were subjected to a simulated pre-calculus oral exam with main questions and follow-up questions. Their performances are compared and the ones with the best and worst performances are identified. The outcome is that the current version of Claude, even though it is an extremely useful tool that has probably recorded the solution to nearly all calculus questions that are available on the Internet, {\em exhibits only a very limited understanding of the subject} and {\em does not exhibit the ability to make intelligent connections} between different features of a pre-calculus mathematics problem that it has never seen before.
tldr: The paper compares the performance of AI software Claude with two humans on high-school level math questions, finding Claude lacks understanding and intelligent connections.
motivation: To assess whether current AI exhibits genuine intelligence or merely pattern matching on familiar problems.
method: A simulated pre-calculus oral exam with novel questions was administered to Claude and two human participants, and their responses were compared.
result: Claude performed poorly on unseen problems, showing limited understanding and inability to make intelligent connections, while humans performed better.
conclusion: Current AI like Claude does not exhibit genuine intelligence or deep understanding of mathematics.

title: Binomial Transform Of Sequences Counting $N$-ary Convexities
authors: Daniil Naumikhin Aidar Dulliev
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the enumeration of [MATH]-ary convex structures on finite sets. Our main result shows that the total number of convexities is expressed as the binomial transform of the sequence of numbers of grounded convexities. We present the exact numbers of all [MATH]-ary and grounded [MATH]-ary convexities for [MATH]. The obtained integer sequences have been cross-referenced with the OEIS. As a result, we identified both known sequences (such as A000798) and new ones not previously listed.
tldr: This paper studies the enumeration of N-ary convexities on finite sets using binomial transforms, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to count the number of convex structures on finite sets, a problem in discrete mathematics and combinatorics.
method: They apply the binomial transform to relate the total number of convexities to the number of grounded convexities, and compute exact numbers for small N.
result: They obtain integer sequences, some known (e.g., A000798) and some new, and cross-reference them with the OEIS.
conclusion: The work contributes to enumerative combinatorics but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Preconditioning For Near-contacts In Large 2d Stokes Flows: A Locally Compressed Method Of Fundamental Solutions
authors: Anna Broms, Anna-Karin Tornberg, Alex H. Barnett
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We tackle two key difficulties in the simulation of the viscous hydrodynamics of a large dense collection of rigid particles: (i) the poor convergence rate of an iterative solution of the discretized linear system as particle gaps shrink, and (ii) the large number of unknowns needed to accurately discretize the resulting lubrication-driven flows. Our focus is the 2D Stokes resistance and mobility boundary value problems for nearly-touching disks. To address both challenges, we introduce a general two-body preconditioning strategy, and implement it with the method of fundamental solutions. For each close particle pair, the hard-to-resolve interaction is represented in a basis precomputed by solving a local boundary value problem on a fine grid. In an iterative solve, the resulting flow field corrects that obtained from a coarse representation of all particles. The local fine-grid correction can even be compressed so that all particles except the pair itself are affected by an equivalent set of coarse sources. Numerical experiments demonstrate rapid GMRES convergence in challenging multi-particle settings, with iteration counts remaining low even in densely packed suspensions. For example, the mobility problem is solved for a random close packing with area fraction [MATH], [MATH] monodisperse disks, and minimum separation [MATH], in just 47 GMRES iterations, achieving five digits of accuracy with 72 vector unknowns per body.
tldr: This paper presents a preconditioning technique for solving Stokes flow problems involving many nearly-touching rigid particles using a method of fundamental solutions.
motivation: Simulating dense suspensions of rigid particles in viscous flow is computationally challenging due to poor iterative solver convergence and high resolution requirements near contacts.
method: A two-body preconditioning strategy is introduced that precomputes local fine-grid corrections for close particle pairs and compresses them into coarse sources affecting all particles.
result: The method achieves rapid GMRES convergence (e.g., 47 iterations for a random close packing with 1000 disks) and high accuracy with only 72 unknowns per body.
conclusion: The proposed preconditioning effectively addresses both convergence and resolution challenges, enabling efficient simulation of large dense suspensions.

title: Existence Of Lebesgue Measurable Functions Outside The Mauldin Hierarchy
authors: Senan Sekhon
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1916, Hausdorff proved that the Baire hierarchy on [MATH], starting with the continuous functions, generates all Borel functions on [MATH]. It remained open whether, starting with the a.e. continuous functions, the corresponding hierarchy generates all Lebesgue measurable functions on [MATH]. We prove that, assuming the Axiom of Choice, the answer is negative.
tldr: This paper proves that the Lebesgue measurable functions are not exhausted by the Mauldin hierarchy, assuming the Axiom of Choice.
motivation: The question of whether the Baire hierarchy starting from a.e. continuous functions generates all Lebesgue measurable functions has been open since 1916.
method: The proof uses set-theoretic techniques, likely involving the Axiom of Choice to construct a Lebesgue measurable function outside the hierarchy.
result: Assuming the Axiom of Choice, there exist Lebesgue measurable functions that are not in the Mauldin hierarchy.
conclusion: The answer to the long-standing problem is negative under ZFC, showing the hierarchy is incomplete.

title: Mjsac: McCormick Relaxation-based Waveform Design For Joint Sensing And Communication
authors: Bodhibrata Mukhopadhyay, Sajid Ahmed, Mohamed-Slim Alouini
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the upcoming 5G Advanced and 6G technologies, joint sensing and communication (JSAC) will play a pivotal role in enabling the simultaneous utilization of hardware and spectrum resources for communication and sensing tasks. While current algorithms primarily focus on designing beampattern invariant covariance matrices for transmitting various symbols for communication, they often overlook the distances among these symbols. While these covariance matrices effectively facilitate ranging operations, they have adverse effects on communication performance. Designing beampattern invariance covariance matrices with maximal distances among themselves poses a challenging non-convex problem. In this paper, we introduce a novel waveform design method based on McCormick relaxation called McCormick-based JSAC (MJSAC). MJSAC sequentially solves an optimization problem to generate a set of covariance matrices by maximizing the distances (Frobenius norm) among themselves while ensuring a consistent beam pattern. Also, MJSAC eliminates the requirement for channel information to generate the covariance matrices. Through simulations, we demonstrate that MJSAC outperforms conventional algorithms, even those utilizing channel information at the transmitter.
tldr: This paper proposes a waveform design method for joint sensing and communication using McCormick relaxation to maximize distances among covariance matrices while maintaining a constant beampattern.
motivation: Existing JSAC algorithms design beampattern-invariant covariance matrices but neglect distances among symbols, harming communication performance. The authors aim to improve communication by maximizing distances among covariance matrices.
method: The method formulates a non-convex optimization problem to maximize Frobenius norm distances among covariance matrices under a constant beampattern constraint, and solves it using McCormick relaxation to handle non-convexity.
result: Simulations show that MJSAC outperforms conventional algorithms, even those using channel information, in terms of communication performance while maintaining sensing capability.
conclusion: MJSAC provides a novel waveform design that enhances communication without requiring channel information, making it suitable for 5G Advanced and 6G systems.

title: Dual Gauss--Legendre Polynomials
authors: Pawe{\l} Wo\'zny
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define and investigate two families of dual polynomials associated with the Gauss--Legendre polynomials, which have recently found interesting applications in computer graphics. Using the presented results, one can derive representations of the Gauss--Legendre polynomials, construct the dual bases for Lagrange bases and solve certain approximation problems arising, for example, in CAGD.
tldr: The paper introduces dual Gauss-Legendre polynomials for applications in computer graphics and CAGD, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To provide mathematical tools for approximation problems in computer-aided geometric design and computer graphics.
method: Defines two families of dual polynomials associated with Gauss-Legendre polynomials and derives their properties.
result: Obtains representations of Gauss-Legendre polynomials and constructs dual bases for Lagrange bases.
conclusion: The dual polynomials are useful for solving approximation problems in CAGD.

title: Maximum Coverage Chase Decoder For Optical Interconnects
authors: Alessandro Cardinale, Wenqing Song, Bin Chen, Alex Alvarado, Andreas Burg, Yifei Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a low-complexity Chase decoder for optical interconnects that formulates test pattern selection as a generalized maximum coverage problem. For concatenated RS-BCH and oFEC codes, our decoder achieves the standard Chase decoding performance with 25% and 61.3% fewer test patterns, respectively.
tldr: A low-complexity Chase decoder for optical interconnects using maximum coverage test pattern selection.
motivation: Optical interconnects require high-speed, low-complexity error correction decoders to meet throughput demands.
method: Formulates test pattern selection as a generalized maximum coverage problem and applies it to concatenated RS-BCH and oFEC codes.
result: Achieves standard Chase decoding performance with 25% and 61.3% fewer test patterns for RS-BCH and oFEC codes respectively.
conclusion: The proposed decoder reduces complexity without sacrificing error correction performance, suitable for optical interconnects.

title: Posterior Consistency Of P\'olya Trees For Deconvolution Under The Linear Model
authors: Asaf Weinstein Nakul Shenoy
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several recent works have addressed the problem of deconvolution under a linear model, where the goal is to estimate a completely unknown [MATH] from a vector of noisy observations [MATH], assuming the coefficients [MATH] are i.i.d. unobserved realizations from [MATH]. Assuming [MATH] has a density [MATH], we study theoretically a Bayesian nonparametric method proposed in Weinstein et al. (2025) that postulates a P\'olya tree prior [MATH] on [MATH] and bases a deconvolution estimate on the posterior distribution [MATH]. Our main result asserts that under the true model (fixed and unknown [MATH]), and under a suitable condition on the minimum eigenvalue of [MATH], the posterior [MATH] concentrates around [MATH] in sup-norm. The analysis presented builds on and extends results from Castillo (2017), where posterior consistency of P\'olya trees was proved for density estimation, the simpler problem of estimating [MATH] when observing the coefficients [MATH] directly.
tldr: This paper proves posterior consistency of Pólya tree priors for deconvolution under a linear model, a Bayesian nonparametric statistics result.
motivation: To provide theoretical guarantees for a Bayesian deconvolution method that estimates an unknown density from noisy observations.
method: The authors analyze the posterior distribution of a Pólya tree prior and prove concentration around the true density in sup-norm under an eigenvalue condition.
result: The posterior is shown to be consistent for deconvolution, extending previous results for direct density estimation.
conclusion: The work validates the Bayesian nonparametric approach for deconvolution problems.

title: Kolmogorov Widths Of An Intersection Of Besov Classes With Dominating Mixed Smoothness In A Besov Space
authors: A. A. Vasil'eva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we obtain order estimates for the Kolmogorov widths of an intersection of a finite family of Besov classes [MATH] with dominating mixed smoothness in a Besov space [MATH] in the case [MATH] when the parameters satisfy certain conditions of general position.
tldr: This paper studies Kolmogorov widths of intersections of Besov classes with dominating mixed smoothness in a Besov space, a topic in approximation theory and functional analysis.
motivation: To obtain order estimates for Kolmogorov widths of intersections of Besov classes, which is a problem in approximation theory.
method: The paper uses techniques from functional analysis and approximation theory to derive order estimates under certain parameter conditions.
result: Order estimates for the Kolmogorov widths are obtained for the intersection of a finite family of Besov classes with dominating mixed smoothness.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of widths in function spaces, but have no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Unbiased Derivative Estimation For Stationary Mean Of Parameterized Markov Chains
authors: Chang-Han Rhee Jeffrey Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new approach to unbiased estimation of the gradients of the stationary means associated with parametrized families of Markov chains. Our estimators are particularly efficient when the Markov chains have slow mixing rate. Our approach does not require a specific parametrization except for an oracle to evaluate the transition density and its gradient at a given data point without any additional knowledge about the density function itself. It makes our estimator suitable for parametrizations associated with neural networks. The estimator can potentially achieve large improvement in terms of efficiency. Numerical experiments confirm the good performance predicted by the theory.
tldr: This paper proposes an unbiased gradient estimation method for stationary means of parameterized Markov chains, with applications to neural network training.
motivation: Gradient estimation for Markov chain stationary distributions is challenging, especially for slow-mixing chains. Existing methods may be biased or inefficient.
method: The authors develop an unbiased estimator that only requires an oracle to evaluate the transition density and its gradient, without full knowledge of the density. The approach leverages a novel variance reduction technique.
result: The estimator achieves unbiasedness and can significantly improve efficiency over existing methods, as demonstrated by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical and efficient tool for gradient estimation in parameterized Markov chains, particularly useful for neural network-based parametrizations.

title: Mean Field Games With Terminal State Constraints
authors: Luciano Campi, Luca Di Persio, Viktorya Vardanyan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a mean field game (MFG) of state and control with state dynamics described by stochastic differential equations driven by both idiosyncratic and common noise, and subject to the constraint that the terminal state variable belongs to a nonempty, convex, closed set. The mean-field interaction enters both the dynamics and the costs through state and control. We formulate an equivalent auxiliary MFG problem and derive the stochastic maximum principle for an auxiliary optimization problem under fixed flows. By means of a suitable forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) of conditional McKean-Vlasov type, we establish a characterization of MFG solutions via such a system. Moreover, we prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the FBSDE system in the specific case where the running cost is zero and the state coefficients are linear. Additionally, we obtain uniqueness results in the sense of Lasry-Lions and we apply our findings to MFGs of optimal investment with a quadratic relative performance criterion.
tldr: This paper studies mean field games with terminal state constraints using stochastic maximum principle and FBSDEs.
motivation: Mean field games model large populations of interacting agents; terminal constraints are important for applications like optimal investment.
method: Formulates an auxiliary MFG problem, derives stochastic maximum principle, and characterizes solutions via conditional McKean-Vlasov FBSDEs.
result: Proves existence and uniqueness for linear state coefficients with zero running cost, and uniqueness in Lasry-Lions sense.
conclusion: Provides a theoretical framework for MFGs with terminal constraints, with potential applications in economics and finance.

title: Expansive Solutions With Prescribed Asymptotics Of The Classical $N$-body Problem
authors: Yutong Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the classical [MATH]-body problem with the [MATH]-type potential, where [MATH]. We construct hyperbolic, parabolic and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions with prescribed asymptotic data as [MATH].
tldr: The paper constructs hyperbolic, parabolic, and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions with prescribed asymptotics for the classical N-body problem with a specific potential.
motivation: To understand the long-term behavior of gravitational systems and classify possible asymptotic motions in the N-body problem.
method: Analytical construction using techniques from celestial mechanics and dynamical systems, likely involving series expansions and asymptotic analysis.
result: Existence of solutions with prescribed asymptotic data as time goes to infinity for the N-body problem with a certain potential.
conclusion: The work extends known results on asymptotic solutions in celestial mechanics, providing a more complete classification.

title: Joint Movable Antenna Positioning And Ris Partitioning For Sum-Rate Maximization
authors: Mohammed Saif
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the utility of the movable antenna (MA) and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) framework for downlink wireless communications. In the considered scenario, a base station (BS) is equipped with two sub-arrays of MAs transmits signals to the users via the RIS. By jointly exploiting the antenna-positioning flexibility of MAs and the RIS element selection capability, the proposed joint MA-RIS framework introduces additional design degrees of freedom to enhance desired signals and mitigate inter-user interference, thereby maximizing the network sum-rate. To this end, we formulate a joint optimization problem involving MA positioning, sub-array beamforming, and RIS element selection, subject to the minimum antenna separation and transmit power constraints. The resulting problem is highly non-convex and challenging to solve directly. To address this issue, an alternating optimization framework is developed that decomposes the problem into three tractable subproblems. Specifically, zero-forcing beamforming is employed for transmit beamformer design, a low-complexity one-dimensional search is derived for RIS element selection, and the MA positioning problem is solved using block coordinate descent (BCD) and convex optimization techniques implemented via CVX. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed joint MA-RIS framework significantly improves the achievable sum-rate compared with conventional fixed MAs and benchmark schemes with random configurations.
tldr: This paper proposes a joint movable antenna positioning and RIS partitioning framework to maximize sum-rate in downlink wireless communications.
motivation: To enhance desired signals and mitigate inter-user interference by exploiting antenna-positioning flexibility and RIS element selection.
method: An alternating optimization framework decomposes the problem into three subproblems: zero-forcing beamforming, low-complexity search for RIS selection, and block coordinate descent for MA positioning.
result: Simulations show significant sum-rate improvement over fixed antennas and benchmark schemes.
conclusion: The joint MA-RIS framework effectively introduces additional design degrees of freedom for wireless communication optimization.

title: A Dynamical Proof Of Non-arithmeticity Of Jordan Spectra
authors: Pratyush Sarkar Hee Oh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a dynamical proof of Benoist's non-arithmeticity theorem for Jordan spectra of Zariski dense subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups. After passing to a Zariski dense Schottky subgroup, we use the coding of the limit set to realize Jordan projections as periods of a vector-valued Busemann return map for an expanding map on the Furstenberg boundary. The key step is to prove that a suitable two-branch asymptotic discrepancy is not locally constant on the limit set. We also show that the same criterion applies beyond Lie groups; in particular, it yields a direct density result for multiplier spectra of hyperbolic rational maps whose Julia set is not contained in a circle.
tldr: This paper provides a dynamical proof of non-arithmeticity of Jordan spectra for Zariski dense subgroups of semisimple Lie groups, with applications to hyperbolic rational maps.
motivation: To prove Benoist's non-arithmeticity theorem using dynamical methods and extend the criterion to broader contexts beyond Lie groups.
method: Uses coding of the limit set of a Schottky subgroup to realize Jordan projections as periods of a vector-valued Busemann return map, then shows a two-branch asymptotic discrepancy is not locally constant.
result: Proves non-arithmeticity of Jordan spectra and obtains a density result for multiplier spectra of hyperbolic rational maps whose Julia set is not contained in a circle.
conclusion: The dynamical approach yields a new proof and generalization of non-arithmeticity results, applicable to dynamical systems beyond Lie groups.

title: Convex Generalized Differentiation At Infinity
authors: Nguyen Mau Nam Nguyen Xuan Duy Bao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a generalized differentiation theory at infinity for convex sets and functions. In particular, we study several fundamental notions of convex analysis at infinity, including tangent cones, normal cones, and subdifferentials. Our work complements the recently developed theories of nonsmooth analysis at infinity by focusing on the convex setting, where these constructions preserve convexity and admit natural connections with recession analysis, polarity, and epigraphical geometry. We show that, in the convex case, many results can be established under weaker assumptions and admit simpler and more explicit representations than those available in the general nonsmooth framework. In addition, we develop calculus rules and geometric characterizations for these constructions and apply them to optimality conditions and attainment criteria for convex optimization problems over unbounded feasible sets. The results obtained in this paper provide new tools for the study of convex sets and functions at infinity and further strengthen the connections between convex analysis, variational analysis, and optimization.
tldr: This paper develops a generalized differentiation theory at infinity for convex sets and functions, focusing on tangent cones, normal cones, and subdifferentials.
motivation: To extend nonsmooth analysis at infinity to the convex setting, where constructions preserve convexity and admit simpler representations.
method: The authors define and study convex tangent cones, normal cones, and subdifferentials at infinity, establishing calculus rules and geometric characterizations.
result: They obtain optimality conditions and attainment criteria for convex optimization problems over unbounded feasible sets.
conclusion: The work provides new tools for convex analysis at infinity and strengthens connections between convex analysis, variational analysis, and optimization.

title: Vision-Language-Action Models Meet World Models: Embodied Agentic Ai For Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
authors: Feibo Jiang, Li Dong, Lei Mao, Kezhi Wang, Cunhua Pan, Dong In Kim, Naofal Al-Dhahir
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-Altitude Wireless Networks (LAWNs), composed of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and other aerial platforms, provide integrated perception, communication, and computation services in low-altitude airspace. However, deploying large generative models in this domain faces three major challenges: 1) Limited embodied action mapping; 2) Inadequate physical environment modeling; 3) Insufficient closed-loop optimization. To address these challenges, this study proposes an Embodied Agentic UAV framework. Centered on a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model as the execution core, the framework establishes an end-to-end embodied decision-making pipeline from multimodal environmental perception to continuous control generation. In addition, a World Model (WM) is introduced to capture the coupling between UAV actions and environmental state evolution, thereby supporting environment prediction, policy verification, and dynamic optimization. Furthermore, memory and reflection mechanisms are incorporated to form an adaptive closed-loop optimization paradigm of decision, execution, evaluation, and update, thereby enhancing the system's autonomous decision-making capability and continual evolution ability in complex dynamic environments. Experimental results validate its effectiveness in enabling robust, predictive, and sustainable autonomous control in LAWNs.
tldr: This paper proposes an embodied agentic UAV framework using Vision-Language-Action models and World Models for autonomous control in low-altitude wireless networks.
motivation: Deploying large generative models in LAWNs faces challenges in embodied action mapping, physical environment modeling, and closed-loop optimization.
method: The framework uses a VLA model for end-to-end decision-making from perception to control, a World Model for environment prediction and policy verification, and memory/reflection mechanisms for adaptive closed-loop optimization.
result: Experimental results validate the framework's effectiveness in enabling robust, predictive, and sustainable autonomous control in LAWNs.
conclusion: The proposed approach addresses key challenges in deploying generative models for UAV control, enhancing autonomous decision-making in complex dynamic environments.

title: Affine Approximation In Finite Nagata Dimension And Applications To Lipschitz-free Spaces
authors: Mingu Jung, Colin Petitjean, Anton\'in Prochazka, Andr\'es Quilis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that if [MATH] is a metric space of Nagata dimension at most [MATH], then there exists an atlas on [MATH] modeled on [MATH] such that every Lipschitz map [MATH] (with values in an arbitrary Banach space [MATH]) can be uniformly approximated by maps that are affine, and thus [MATH]-smooth, with respect to this atlas. The construction relies on random metric partitions and stochastic retractions inside Lipschitz-free spaces. As an application, we introduce approximate continuous upper gradient [MATH]-structures (ACUG [MATH]-structures) on metric spaces and prove that every space of finite Nagata dimension carries an ACUG structure modeled on a superreflexive Banach space. Finally, adapting a proof due to Bourgain, we show that if [MATH] has an ACUG superreflexive-structure, then the Lipschitz-free space [MATH] has Pelczy\'nski's property (V*). In particular, at least in the compact case, our result recovers all previously known examples of metric spaces [MATH] for which [MATH] has property (V*).
tldr: This paper studies affine approximations on metric spaces of finite Nagata dimension and their applications to Lipschitz-free spaces, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the concept of affine approximation to metric spaces with finite Nagata dimension, which is a purely mathematical problem in functional analysis and metric geometry.
method: They use random metric partitions and stochastic retractions inside Lipschitz-free spaces to construct an atlas that allows uniform approximation of Lipschitz maps by affine maps.
result: They prove that every metric space of finite Nagata dimension admits an ACUG superreflexive-structure, and that the Lipschitz-free space over such a space has Pelczyński's property (V*).
conclusion: The work provides new structural results in Banach space theory and metric geometry, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: High-order Multi-structures-preserving Exponential Integrators For The Derivative Nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger Equation
authors: Liping Wu, Li Yang, Chaolong Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a novel class of high-order mass-, energy- and momentum-preserving exponential integrators for solving the derivative nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation. Firstly, we reformulate the original system into an exponential supplementary variable system based on the idea of the exponential supplementary variable approach, and then the reformulated system is discretized by using the standard Fourier pseudo-spectral method in space and the high-order prediction and correction Lawson Runge-Kutta method in time, respectively. The proposed method is highly efficient, temporally high-order accurate, and simultaneously preserves the mass, energy and momentum in the discrete setting. Finally, numerical experiments validate the accuracy and energy-preserving properties.
tldr: This paper develops high-order structure-preserving exponential integrators for the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation, focusing on numerical methods for partial differential equations.
motivation: To design efficient numerical schemes that preserve multiple invariants (mass, energy, momentum) for the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation, which is important for long-time simulations.
method: The authors reformulate the equation into an exponential supplementary variable system, discretize in space using Fourier pseudo-spectral method, and use high-order prediction-correction Lawson Runge-Kutta methods in time.
result: The proposed integrators achieve high temporal accuracy and simultaneously preserve mass, energy, and momentum in discrete settings, validated by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The new class of exponential integrators offers an efficient and accurate approach for solving the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation while preserving key physical invariants.

title: Non-special Divisors, LCPs Of Codes, And Lcd Codes On Kummer Extensions
authors: Chang-An Zhao Huachao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, constructions of linear complementary pairs (LCPs) of codes and linear complementary dual (LCD) codes on function fields have attracted considerable attention due to the wide range of applications of these codes. Such constructions rely on non-special divisors of degrees [MATH] and [MATH]. In this work, we investigate Kummer extensions defined by [MATH] with [MATH] and establish an arithmetic characterization of non-special divisors whose support can contain non-totally ramified places. Based on this characterization, we explicitly construct non-special divisors of degree [MATH] on the GK curve. Moreover, utilizing pure gaps, we explicitly provide several families of effective non-special divisors of degree [MATH] on Kummer extensions with the same multiplicities. We then develop a general framework for constructing LCPs of algebraic geometry (AG) codes on Kummer extensions. By virtue of canonical divisors, we show that the security parameters of LCPs of AG codes can be determined within this framework, which also enables the construction of LCD AG codes. Finally, we illustrate our results with representative examples, including LCPs of codes on the GK curve and LCD codes on quotients of the Hermitian curve.
tldr: This paper constructs linear complementary pairs (LCPs) and linear complementary dual (LCD) codes on Kummer extensions using non-special divisors, with applications to algebraic geometry codes.
motivation: To develop new constructions of LCPs and LCD codes on function fields, which have applications in cryptography and coding theory.
method: The authors characterize non-special divisors on Kummer extensions and use pure gaps to construct effective non-special divisors, then build a framework for LCPs of AG codes.
result: They provide explicit constructions of non-special divisors on the GK curve and Kummer extensions, and show how to determine security parameters of LCPs using canonical divisors.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of LCPs and LCD codes on algebraic curves, with examples on the GK curve and Hermitian curve quotients.

title: Segment-Wise Soft Robotics Inspired Flexible Antenna Arrays: Design And Optimization
authors: Shuaishuai Han, Konstantinos Ntougias, Elio Faddoul, Ioannis Krikidis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a segment-wise soft robotic antenna (SRA) system, where each soft robotic arm referred to as a tentacle, comprises multiple independently controllable segments with bending, elongation-retraction, and sweeping motions. By adjusting segment motion parameters, the positions of surface-mounted antennas are reconfigured, distinguishing it from conventional reconfigurable antenna (RA) systems. Based on this model, we propose two antenna deployment schemes: the segmented end-antenna configuration (SEAC), where fixed antennas are mounted at the segment ends and reconfigured via segment motions; and the hybrid end-and-intermediate antenna configuration (HEIAC), where RAs are further integrated as intra-segment antennas. In HEIAC, soft-robot segment deformation provides large-scale spatial reconfiguration, while RAs enable fine-grained adjustment. For SEAC, we formulate a sum-rate maximization problem accounting for inter-segment connectivity and the nonlinear mapping from segment deformation parameters to antenna coordinates, and develop a penalty dual decomposition-projected gradient ascent (PDD-PGA) algorithm. For HEIAC, we jointly optimize segment deformation, intra-segment antenna positions, and antenna activation using a block coordinate descent (BCD)-PDD-PGA algorithm with greedy backward antenna selection. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed schemes substantially outperform fixed-position antenna arrays and conventional RA baselines. In particular, SEAC and HEIAC achieve 37.9% and 32.1% sum-rate gains over conventional 3D reconfigurable arrays, respectively, while SEAC provides up to a 49.3% gain in compact array deployments.
tldr: This paper designs and optimizes flexible antenna arrays using soft robotics for reconfigurable antenna systems.
motivation: Conventional reconfigurable antennas have limited flexibility; soft robotics enables large-scale spatial reconfiguration of antenna positions.
method: Two deployment schemes (SEAC and HEIAC) are proposed, with optimization algorithms (PDD-PGA and BCD-PDD-PGA) to maximize sum-rate.
result: The proposed schemes achieve up to 49.3% sum-rate gain over conventional 3D reconfigurable arrays.
conclusion: Soft robotic antennas offer significant performance improvements for wireless communication systems.

title: Curvature-Induced Force Fields In Hyperelasticity
authors: Victor Dods
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Originally motivated by creating first-person computer visualizations within Riemannian manifolds -- the author was led to study deformable-body mechanics, as rigid-body mechanics is not available in a generic Riemannian manifold due to its lack of nontrivial isometry group. Hyperelasticity is a particularly nice sub-category of continuum mechanics in which a deformable, elastic body's behavior is determined by a stored energy density function. This allows problems to be posed variationally, and powerful tools brought to bear on studying and solving them. This article presents numerical simulations of static solutions to a particular class of problems in hyperelastic mechanics in 2-dimensional Riemannian manifolds in which a flat hyperelastic body [MATH] is embedded into a region [MATH] in a nowhere-flat surface [MATH] of revolution [MATH] such that [MATH] decreases as [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the Gaussian curvature of [MATH]. For example, the funnel [MATH] or the paraboloid [MATH]. Because [MATH] is flat, the body can't achieve a zero-stored-energy configuration, and restorative forces arise in the body to move it toward a region of lower stored energy -- meaning, toward a flatter configuration. With the addition of a gravitational potential [MATH] on [MATH], forces act on the body to pull it toward [MATH]. If the body has sufficient stiffness and remains within the region [MATH], then the body has an equilibrium configuration in which the body's deformation-response forces perfectly cancel the gravitational forces. Such a configuration represents a kind of "levitation" phenomenon within this surface. The numerical implementation of this problem will be detailed and the resulting numerical solutions and various consequences discussed.
tldr: This paper studies hyperelastic deformations in curved Riemannian manifolds, leading to curvature-induced force fields and levitation phenomena.
motivation: To understand deformable-body mechanics in generic Riemannian manifolds where rigid-body mechanics is unavailable, and to simulate static solutions for hyperelastic bodies embedded in curved surfaces.
method: Numerical simulations of static solutions for a flat hyperelastic body embedded in a nowhere-flat surface of revolution, using variational principles and a stored energy density function.
result: The body experiences restorative forces toward flatter regions, and with added gravitational potential, equilibrium configurations exhibit a levitation-like effect where deformation forces cancel gravity.
conclusion: Curvature can induce effective force fields on deformable bodies, leading to novel equilibrium phenomena such as levitation in curved spaces.

title: Last-Iterate Convergence Of Optimistic Multiplicative Weight Update
authors: Francesco Orabona
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimistic Gradient Descent Ascent (OGDA) and Optimistic Multiplicative-Weights Update (OMWU) are two very popular algorithms to solve convex/concave saddle-point problems, where OMWU is the non-Euclidean, entropic version of OGDA. It is known since the '80s that the last iterate of OGDA asymptotically converges to a saddle point in smooth problems. On the other hand, it is unknown if OMWU has the same property. In this paper, I show that OMWU converges asymptotically for smooth convex-concave saddle-point problems, with a small enough constant learning rate. The result does not require uniqueness, strict complementarity, an error bound, or initialization near a solution. The main new ingredient is a boundary argument showing that every cluster point satisfies the inactive-coordinate KKT inequalities. The boundary argument was discovered with assistance from ChatGPT and is documented in the appendix.
tldr: This paper proves last-iterate convergence of Optimistic Multiplicative Weights Update for smooth convex-concave saddle-point problems.
motivation: It was unknown whether OMWU, the entropic version of OGDA, enjoys last-iterate convergence like OGDA does.
method: The author uses a boundary argument to show that every cluster point satisfies inactive-coordinate KKT inequalities, with assistance from ChatGPT.
result: OMWU converges asymptotically for smooth convex-concave saddle-point problems with a small enough constant learning rate, without requiring uniqueness or strict complementarity.
conclusion: OMWU is a provably convergent algorithm for saddle-point problems, closing a gap in the optimization literature.

title: bAdag: An Adaptive Block Coordinate Gradient Method For Smooth Nonconvex Functions
authors: Giovanni Seraghiti
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A new Block Coordinate Gradient (BCG) method, dubbed bAdag, for smooth, nonconvex minimization problem is proposed; it falls in the class of Objective Function Free Optimization (OFFO) methods, and it is based on the AdaGrad algorithm. At each iteration, our method computes an adaptive step size based on the cumulative sum of block gradients, instead of full gradients as in AdaGrad-type methods. We prove ergodic, sublinear convergence rates for the bAdag algorithm when minimizing a smooth, possibly nonconvex objective under the (block) Lipschitz continuity assumption on the gradient. Our theory covers three widely popular block selection strategies: the Cyclic (C) rule, Uniform Random selection (UR), and the greedy Gauss-Southwell (GS) rule. We also extend our algorithm and its convergence theory to box-constrained smooth functions. We validate the proposed algorithms through synthetic and real-world experiments.
tldr: This paper proposes a block coordinate gradient method for smooth nonconvex optimization, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The authors aim to develop an adaptive step-size block coordinate gradient method that is objective-function-free and efficient for large-scale nonconvex problems.
method: The method, bAdag, computes adaptive step sizes based on cumulative block gradients and supports cyclic, uniform random, and Gauss-Southwell block selection rules.
result: Ergodic sublinear convergence rates are proved for smooth nonconvex functions under block Lipschitz continuity, and the method is extended to box-constrained problems.
conclusion: bAdag provides a theoretically grounded and practically effective optimization algorithm validated on synthetic and real-world data.

title: Splitting Strategies For The Fully-coupled Nonlinear Thermo-hydro-mechanical Problem
authors: Stefano Bonetti, Michele Botti, Paola F. Antonietti
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose novel semi-decoupled and fully-decoupled iterative algorithms for efficiently solving the fully-coupled nonlinear four-field thermo-poroelastic model discretized in space by discontinuous Galerkin method on polytopal grids. We present the model problem, its four-field formulation, and the arbitrary-order weighted symmetric interior penalty scheme exploited for its spatial discretization. Such a scheme is robust with respect to strong heterogeneities in the model coefficients. Then, we present the two solution strategies and prove that under suitable conditions both schemes are convergent. A wide set of numerical simulations is presented to assess the convergence and robustness properties of the proposed method. Moreover, we test the scheme with literature and physically sound test cases for proof-of-concept applications in the geophysical context.
tldr: This paper presents iterative algorithms for solving a fully-coupled nonlinear thermo-hydro-mechanical model discretized with discontinuous Galerkin methods on polytopal grids, with applications in geophysics.
motivation: Efficiently solving coupled nonlinear multiphysics problems is computationally challenging, especially for large-scale geophysical applications.
method: The authors propose semi-decoupled and fully-decoupled iterative algorithms for the four-field thermo-poroelastic model, using a weighted symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin scheme for spatial discretization.
result: Convergence of both schemes is proved under suitable conditions, and numerical simulations demonstrate robustness and efficiency on heterogeneous problems and benchmark tests.
conclusion: The proposed splitting strategies provide efficient and convergent solvers for fully-coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical problems, suitable for geophysical simulations.

title: On Finding Exact Solutions Of Linear Programs In The Oracle Model
authors: Daniel Dadush, L\'aszl\'o A. V\'egh, Giacomo Zambelli
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider linear programming in the oracle model: [MATH], where the polyhedron [MATH] is given by a separation oracle. We present an algorithm that finds exact primal and dual solutions using [MATH] oracle calls and [MATH] arithmetic operations, where [MATH] is a geometric condition number associated with the system [MATH]. These bounds do not depend on the cost vector [MATH] and do not require a priori knowledge of [MATH]. For rational data, [MATH] is polynomially bounded in the encoding size of [MATH], thus providing a polynomial-time algorithm. The algorithm works in a black box manner, requiring a subroutine for approximate primal and dual solutions; the above running times are achieved when using the cutting plane method of Jiang, Lee, Song, and Wong (STOC 2020) for this subroutine. Whereas approximate solvers may return primal solutions only, we develop a general framework for extracting dual certificates based on the work of Burrell and Todd (Math. Oper. Res. 1985). Our algorithm strengthens results by Gr\"otschel, Lov\'asz, and Schrijver (Prog. Comb. Opt. 1984), and by Frank and Tardos (Combinatorica 1987) that rely on bit-complexity arguments. Our algorithm avoids rounding-based arguments such as simultaneous Diophantine approximation and uses geometric arguments instead.
tldr: This paper presents an algorithm for solving linear programs in the oracle model with exact primal and dual solutions, using geometric condition numbers instead of bit-complexity arguments.
motivation: Classical algorithms for linear programming in the oracle model rely on bit-complexity or rounding, which may be inefficient or require a priori knowledge. The authors aim to develop a purely geometric approach that avoids these limitations.
method: The algorithm uses a cutting plane method for approximate solutions and a general framework based on Burrell and Todd to extract exact dual certificates. It operates in a black-box manner, requiring only a separation oracle.
result: The algorithm achieves O(m log(χ_A)) oracle calls and O(m^3 log(χ_A)) arithmetic operations, where χ_A is a geometric condition number. For rational data, this yields a polynomial-time algorithm.
conclusion: The work provides a new geometric perspective on exact linear programming in the oracle model, strengthening previous results and avoiding rounding-based arguments.

title: Distributionally Robust Reinsurance Under Robust Optimized Certainty Equivalent Risk Measure
authors: Xinqiao Xie, Taizhong Hu, Tiantian Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a class of preference robust risk measures- (ROCE)-which encompasses several widely used measures, including Conditional Value-at-Risk and expectiles, as special cases. Motivated by recent developments in distributionally robust optimal reinsurance (DROR), we investigate DROR problems under the ROCE risk measure and consider two prominent uncertainty sets: the mean-variance uncertainty set and the Wasserstein uncertainty set. For the mean-variance uncertainty set, we reformulate the infinite-dimensional optimization problem into a finite-dimensional one by showing that it suffices to consider three-point distributions. This leads to a unified and explicit formulation for a broad class of ROCE risk measures and offers a simplified framework that also recovers earlier results for Conditional Value-at-Risk and expectiles. For the Wasserstein uncertainty set, we also derive a tractable finite-dimensional formulation. The resulting data-driven models enable efficient computation and facilitate a systematic comparison between moment-based and Wasserstein-based uncertainty sets in the optimal deductible design. Numerical experiments are exhibited to illustrate the performance of our reformulated programs.
tldr: This paper studies distributionally robust reinsurance optimization under a robust risk measure, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to extend distributionally robust optimization to reinsurance problems using a flexible risk measure that generalizes CVaR and expectiles.
method: They reformulate infinite-dimensional optimization problems into finite-dimensional ones for mean-variance and Wasserstein uncertainty sets, proving that three-point distributions suffice for the former.
result: Unified explicit formulations are derived for a broad class of risk measures, and tractable data-driven models are obtained for both uncertainty sets.
conclusion: The proposed framework enables efficient computation and systematic comparison of moment-based and Wasserstein-based uncertainty sets in optimal deductible design.

title: Descriptions Of Traces Of Weighted Sobolev Spaces To Ahlfors--David Regular Sets In The Case $p=1$
authors: Alexander Tyulenev
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given [MATH], an Ahlors--David [MATH]-regular set [MATH], and a weight [MATH] satisfying the local Muckenhoupt [MATH]-condition, we present a complete intrinsic description of the trace-space [MATH] of the weighted first-order Sobolev space [MATH] to [MATH]. Furthermore, we construct a new family of nonlinear bounded extension operators acting from [MATH] to [MATH]. Finally, we find conditions on [MATH] that sufficient for the existence of a bounded linear extension operator from [MATH] to [MATH].
tldr: This paper provides a complete intrinsic description of traces of weighted Sobolev spaces to Ahlfors-David regular sets for p=1.
motivation: Understanding trace spaces of Sobolev functions on rough sets is fundamental in analysis and PDEs, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The author uses weighted Sobolev spaces with local Muckenhoupt weights and constructs nonlinear bounded extension operators, building on prior trace theory for p>1.
result: A complete intrinsic description of the trace space is given, and conditions for existence of a bounded linear extension operator are found.
conclusion: The work advances harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Testing Axial Symmetry In Multivariate Location-scale Linear Regression
authors: Miroslav \v{s}iman \v{s}\'arka Hudecov\'a
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article deals with the problem of testing conditional axial symmetry within a~multivariate linear heteroscedastic regression framework. A new test based on integrated rank scores is introduced and its asymptotic distribution is derived. The proposed method extends a similar procedure developed for multivariate data to the regression setting. The test may also be employed to assess specific hypotheses concerning distributional properties of the error term. Its performance and application is illustrated in a small simulation study and with real economic data. The article also contains a few theoretical results regarding axial symmetry that may be of independent interest.
tldr: This paper proposes a new test for conditional axial symmetry in multivariate linear regression, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To extend testing of axial symmetry from multivariate data to a regression framework, addressing distributional properties of error terms.
method: Introduces a test based on integrated rank scores and derives its asymptotic distribution.
result: The test is validated through simulation and applied to real economic data; some theoretical results on axial symmetry are also provided.
conclusion: The proposed test is a useful tool for assessing axial symmetry in regression, but it is purely classical statistics.

title: Game-Theoretic Foundations Of Competition For Conscious Access
authors: Efthyvoulos Drousiotis, Paul Spirakis, Sotiris Nikoletseas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.11242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conscious access in the human brain is often described as the outcome of a competition among candidate representations, but this competition is usually left at the level of mechanism or metaphor rather than analyzed as a strategic allocation problem. We introduce an access contest in which internal modules compete for a scarce broadcast slot by choosing a costly amplification effort. Access is allocated by a smooth probabilistic rule, allowing the model to interpolate between diffuse selection and winner-take-all competition. We establish pure-strategy equilibrium existence under standard convexity and bounded-benefit assumptions, and give sufficient conditions for uniqueness using diagonal strict concavity. We then analyze capture in the two-module case, and for quadratic costs, we derive a sharp threshold in the competition intensity above which capture occurs. For strongly convex costs, we prove an if-and-only-if capture criterion in terms of the cost-adjusted amplification advantage of the lower-value module. Under the same curvature-dominance condition that guarantees uniqueness, we show that the unique pure Nash equilibrium of the general \(M\)-module access contest can be approximated efficiently by projected pseudo-gradient dynamics, with logarithmic dependence on the desired accuracy. Finally, we prove an impossibility theorem for single-slot access mechanisms. Exact winner-take-all efficiency is incompatible with robustness to small score perturbations. Thus, smooth probabilistic access rules are not merely analytically convenient, but structurally motivated. These results provide a game-theoretic foundation for studying competition for conscious access, connecting equilibrium analysis, capture, computation, and mechanism-level limitations under a common formal model.
